scope.instruction:
# Security audit target: Flames (Android AI agent client, Flutter/Dart + Kotlin)

## What this app is
A mobile "AI agent workstation". It talks to a REMOTE LLM API (OpenAI-compatible) and to a
remote Hermes Gateway (WebSocket JSON-RPC + SSE), runs a ReAct tool-calling loop on the
device, and can call native Android capabilities as agent tools (clipboard, location,
camera, calendar, notifications, Health Connect, accessibility tree reading, NFC).

You are auditing the FULL repository at the mount root. There is NO running app instance,
NO emulator, NO adb. This is a WHITE-BOX SOURCE-ONLY audit.

## Critical honesty rule
Any finding that would normally require a running app to demonstrate MUST be labelled
"unconfirmed, not dynamically validated" in your report. Do NOT claim a finding is
exploitable if you could not execute it. Static evidence (file:line + code path) is
required for every finding. A plausible-sounding but unproven finding is worse than no
finding.

## Trust boundaries (this is where the money is)
1. **Secrets at rest**: user API key / `API_SERVER_KEY` and server profiles.
   See `lib/data/datasources/local/settings/secure_storage_service.dart` and
   `lib/common/injection/modules.dart` (FlutterSecureStorage / EncryptedSharedPreferences).
   Check: is anything sensitive written to plain SharedPreferences, Hive, SQLite, logs,
   crash reports, or exported files instead?
2. **Secrets in transit / in logs**: grep for any code path that logs, prints, shows in a
   toast/snackbar, or serializes an API key, bearer token, or Authorization header.
   Interpolated strings in `dart:developer log()`, `print()`, `debugPrint()` count.
3. **Server profile from QR pairing**: `lib/domain/entities/pairing/`,
   `lib/presentation/screen/pairing/qr_scanner_screen.dart`. A QR payload is attacker
   controlled (anyone can print/paste a QR). Check: can a hostile QR payload redirect the
   client's API key to an attacker-controlled base URL? Is the base URL scheme validated
   (https-only)? Is there a same-origin / allowlist check before the stored key is sent?
   This is the highest-value attack chain in this app - trace it end to end.
4. **Inbound notifications**: `FlamesNotificationListenerService` reads other apps'
   notifications. Check whether notification text can reach the agent prompt / a tool
   result / the UI without being treated as untrusted data (prompt injection surface).
5. **Share intent / files / clipboard**: `MainActivity` has exported SEND, SEND_MULTIPLE
   and VIEW intent-filters. Check for path traversal, arbitrary file read, intent
   redirection, and whether `content://` URIs are validated before being read or uploaded.
6. **Agent tool layer**: `lib/domain/tools/chat/tool_registry.dart` and
   `lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/`. Tools are tiered (Tier 1 auto / Tier 2 permission /
   Tier 3 HITL). Check: can a tool be invoked from remote model output without passing its
   tier gate? Can the tier be downgraded by remote/untrusted input (e.g. a remote skill
   package, a tool result, or a gateway RPC message)?

## Concrete targets to inspect
- `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`: every `android:exported="true"` component
  (MainActivity, FlamesNotificationListenerService, FlamesAccessibilityService,
  FlamesQuickTile, RationaleActivity, ViewPermissionUsageActivity alias). For each, decide
  whether it is exported ONLY because a system permission guards it
  (BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE / BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE /
  BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE / START_VIEW_PERMISSION_USAGE) or whether it is reachable by a
  third-party app. `MainActivity` and `RationaleActivity` are NOT permission-guarded -
  analyse what a malicious app can do with them (intent extras, deep links, launch params).
  Also: no `network_security_config` and no `usesCleartextTraffic` attribute are present.
  State the consequence honestly (Android 9+ defaults to cleartext blocked) and whether
  any code path uses `http://`.
- `lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/piper_tts_engine.dart`: downloads a Piper TTS voice
  tarball over HTTPS, verifies MD5, extracts it to disk. MD5 is not a collision-resistant
  integrity primitive and the expected digest comes from a manifest. Assess: where does the
  expected MD5 come from, is the download URL validated, and can a tampered tarball pass
  verification (e.g. tar path traversal / zip-slip on extraction, symlink escape)?
- `lib/data/datasources/local/memory/sqlite_memory_datasource.dart`: memory vault using
  SQLite FTS5. Check for SQL injection via FTS MATCH query building, and whether stored
  memory content is treated as trusted when replayed into a prompt.
- WebSocket / SSE clients: `lib/data/datasources/remote/gateway/` and any SSE parser.
  Check TLS/WSS enforcement, certificate handling, reconnect auth, and whether the gateway
  URL is validated before a stored bearer token is attached to it.
- `lib/domain/services/skills/` (remote skill package loader) and
  `lib/presentation/screen/skills/`: a downloaded skill package is attacker-controlled text
  that becomes part of the system prompt. Check whether anything from it can reach a tool
  invocation, and whether imported skills are enabled by default.
- Release/build hygiene: is `android:debuggable`, a debug-only provider, a backup rule
  (`android:allowBackup` defaults to true when unset - check and report), or a logging
  endpoint left enabled? Check `android/app/build.gradle.kts` for signing/minify settings.

## What is OUT of scope
- Anything in `.worktrees/` (do not exist here), `build/`, `third_party/` vendored code
  unless the app calls into it directly.
- iOS/macOS/Linux/Windows platform folders except for a quick check of anything that
  contradicts the Android finding (say so if you skip them).
- Dependency CVEs in `pubspec.lock` (report only if a pinned version is known-vulnerable
  AND the vulnerable code path is actually reachable from this app - otherwise say it is
  out of scope).

## Deliverable
Standard Strix output: `vulnerabilities.json` + `vulnerabilities/<id>.md` + `findings.sarif`.
For each finding include: exact file:line, root cause, the concrete attack path (who is the
attacker, what do they control, what do they get), and a remediation. Confidence field must
reflect that no dynamic validation was possible.

agents.task:
WHITE-BOX SOURCE-ONLY audit of Flames Android Flutter app at /workspace/flames-audit-t196 (real repo /tmp/flames-audit-t196). NO emulator, NO adb, NO running app. Every finding is static: confidence at most "medium" and the report MUST say "unconfirmed, not dynamically validated".

FIRST call get_threat_model(target="/workspace/flames-audit-t196") and read it.

IMPORTANT SCOPE BOUNDARY: another agent already owns the exported-component / manifest / BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE permission analysis of `FlamesAccessibilityService.kt`. Do NOT report anything about exported components, permission guards, or whether a malicious app can bind to the service. YOUR scope is the DATA FLOW: what the service collects, where it goes, and how the receiving side treats it.

YOUR JOB: independently validate (or refute) the data-flow candidates below, then file with create_vulnerability_report ONLY the ones that hold.

=== CANDIDATE A (primary): screen text from ANY app reaches the model with no untrusted-data framing ===
Evidence already gathered (verify every line yourself, do not trust me):
- `android/app/src/main/kotlin/ai/hermes/flames/FlamesAccessibilityService.kt:51-112` — `captureTree()` does a BFS from `rootInActiveWindow` and emits, per node, `"text" to (node.text?.toString() ?: "")` (line 76) and `"contentDescription"` (line 77) plus `"packageName"` (line 78). It is a PULL model: nothing is pushed to Dart on accessibility events (`onAccessibilityEvent` at line 120-122 only records `lastEventPackage`). Confirm that there is no continuous push/upload.
- `android/app/src/main/res/xml/accessibility_service_config.xml:5` — `flagRetrieveInteractiveWindows` + `flagIncludeNotImportantViews`; line 6 `canRetrieveWindowContent="true"`. So the tree of the foreground app (ANY app, including a malicious one's own window) is readable.
- Dart side: `lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/accessibility_inspector_service.dart:41-55` `getScreenTree()` → `lib/domain/tools/chat/accessibility_inspector_service.dart:257-298` `AccessibilityTreeSerializer.serialize()` builds plain text lines `- [role] "label" clickable ...` → returned as a tool result.
- Tool registration: `lib/domain/tools/chat/tool_registry.dart:1715-1775`, tool name `ui_find_elements`, `securityTier: SecurityTier.tier2Permission` (line 1760), and a comment at 1761-1763 stating there is deliberately NO `checkPermission` gate.
- Tool results reach the model as `role: 'tool'` messages: `lib/presentation/screen/chat/cubit/agent_cubit.dart:820-825`.
- THE ASYMMETRY: the codebase HAS a prompt-injection scanner — `lib/domain/services/skills/skill_security_scanner.dart` (patterns for `ignore_previous_instructions`, `disregard_system_prompt`, `exfiltrate`, `send_credentials_out`, chatml delimiters `<|im_start|>`, etc.) — but it is applied ONLY to imported skill text. Confirm by grepping the whole repo for every caller of `SkillSecurityScanner`. Nothing scans accessibility-tree text, notification text, web-page text, or memory text.

Verify or refute, adversarially:
- Does any code path apply an injection filter, sanitisation, or untrusted-data wrapper to the accessibility tree before it reaches the prompt? (`_sanitize` at `lib/domain/tools/chat/accessibility_inspector_service.dart:320-322` only strips newlines/tabs and replaces `"` with `'` for display formatting — confirm that this is NOT an injection control.)
- Is the tree auto-captured on every turn, or only when the model explicitly calls the tool? Confirm it is explicit-call-only (that materially lowers severity — say so).
- Who realistically controls the text? Any app in the foreground whose UI the user views while the agent runs. A malicious app can render a screen and wait. State this attacker story precisely and note the required precondition (user must have granted the accessibility permission AND the agent must read the screen).

=== CANDIDATE B (secondary, weaker — assess honestly): no password-field redaction ===
- `captureTree()` never calls `AccessibilityNodeInfo.isPassword()`. Grep the entire `android/` and `lib/` trees for `isPassword` to confirm it appears nowhere.
- Assess honestly: Android may itself redact password text before an accessibility service sees it, and that behaviour is device/OEM dependent. You have NO device to test on. So: state the *missing control* (the code makes no attempt to exclude password/secure fields) as the observation, and be explicit that whether the platform already redacts is UNVERIFIED here. Do NOT claim "passwords are captured" as an established fact. If you cannot establish actual secret capture, this candidate does not meet the bar for a vulnerability report on its own — fold it in as an observation/assumption inside Candidate A's report or record it as needs_follow_up. Do not file it as a separate inflated finding.

IF CANDIDATE A HOLDS: call create_vulnerability_report with target "/workspace/flames-audit-t196". It MUST include `code_locations` (repo-relative paths, 1-based line numbers verified against the real files) with verbatim `fix_before`/`fix_after` pairs, plus `fix_verification` and `fix_pr_body`. Fix shape (derive it yourself, keep it minimal and repo-native): wrap accessibility-tree output in explicit untrusted-data framing AND/OR run it through the existing `SkillSecurityScanner` before it becomes a tool result — reuse the existing scanner, do not invent a new one. The Kotlin-side redaction of password/secure nodes (`isPassword()` / secure-window filtering in `captureTree`) is a legitimate second part of the fix; if you include it, use a SEPARATE code_location entry with verbatim `fix_before` matching `FlamesAccessibilityService.kt` exactly (indentation matters — the file uses 4-space Kotlin indentation, verify by reading it).
`fix_verification`: run what you can (`dart analyze lib/...` on touched Dart files, `flutter test` for any test touching these files — check `test/` for an existing accessibility test to run) and mark every gate you could only reason about as an explicit gap. The Kotlin side cannot be compiled here if there is no Android SDK — say so plainly instead of claiming it compiles.
- confidence: "medium" max with confidence_rationale naming the gap (no device, no model, no end-to-end run). counterevidence = strongest real case against (explicit-call-only, the model may ignore injected text, the permission prerequisite). severity_change_conditions = the one piece of evidence that would move it.

IF IT DOES NOT HOLD: do NOT file. Name the specific control (file:line) and call record_coverage(outcome="ruled_out", ...) on surface "accessibility tree (ui_find_elements) → model prompt". Otherwise record_coverage(outcome="needs_follow_up"). Never silently drop.

Report back via agent_finish with what you confirmed, what you refuted, and what is left open.

WHITE-BOX SOURCE-ONLY audit of the Flames Android Flutter app at /workspace/flames-audit-t196 (real repo /tmp/flames-audit-t196, mounted read-write).

FIRST: call get_threat_model(target="/workspace/flames-audit-t196") and read it — shared baseline. Record coverage with record_coverage as you go.

YOUR MISSION — **sensitive device data flows into the agent**. Where does highly sensitive data (screen content, health data, location, camera frames, NFC payloads, contacts) go, and can untrusted content from those sources reach the agent prompt as instructions?

NOTE ON OVERLAP (do not duplicate): another agent owns the exported-component/permission analysis of FlamesAccessibilityService.kt, FlamesHealthConnect.kt and the manifest. YOU own the **data flow** — where the collected data goes and how it is treated.

FILES YOU OWN:
- android/app/src/main/kotlin/ai/hermes/flames/FlamesAccessibilityService.kt (the DATA it collects and where it is pushed)
- android/app/src/main/res/xml/accessibility_service_config.xml
- android/app/src/main/kotlin/ai/hermes/flames/FlamesHealthConnect.kt
- the Dart-side consumers: lib/data/datasources/tools/device/ (accessibility, health, location, camera, nfc, contacts services) and lib/domain/tools/device/
- lib/presentation/screen/external_camera/ and its cubit

REQUIRED ANALYSIS (exact file:line per claim):
1. Accessibility tree: what exactly is captured (window content, text of all visible nodes)? Is it pushed to Dart continuously or on demand? Where does it end up — a tool result, a prompt, a remote upload? Is there any redaction of password fields / sensitive views?
2. Prompt-injection via screen content: the accessibility tree of ANY app (including a malicious app's own window) is attacker-controlled text. Trace whether it is marked as untrusted data or concatenated into the agent prompt as trusted content. This is the same class as notification injection — determine whether the code does anything different for it.
3. Health Connect: which record types are read, is the read permission-gated in code (not just manifest), and where is the data sent? Is it included in prompts by default?
4. Location / camera / contacts / NFC: same questions — is the data sent to a remote LLM/gateway by default, and is there a user-visible indication? Is any of it cached or logged?
5. For each source, determine whether the DATA can reach a remote endpoint that is NOT the user's configured server (i.e. is there any hardcoded or config-driven alternate endpoint?).
6. Check the external camera feature specifically: does it stream/upload camera frames anywhere, and to which URL? Is the URL user-configured and validated?
7. Any continuous/background collection (a service that keeps reading the accessibility tree or health data)? Check FlamesBackgroundService.kt for what it does while running.

DELIVERABLE:
- For each CONCRETE candidate, spawn a focused child agent to independently validate and, if it holds, file with create_vulnerability_report including the inline fix (code_locations with verbatim fix_before/fix_after + fix_verification + fix_pr_body). NO dynamic validation is possible (no emulator/adb, no running app) — confidence at most "medium" and the report MUST state "unconfirmed, not dynamically validated".
- Candidates that do NOT hold: name the specific control (file:line) → record_coverage(outcome="ruled_out"). Cannot name one → outcome="needs_follow_up". Never silently drop.
- agent_finish with summary + open_items.

Be honest: a permission-gated sensitive-data flow to the user's OWN configured server is expected app behavior, not a vulnerability. The finding is when data goes somewhere unexpected, is exposed beyond the user, or when attacker-controlled text gains instruction authority.

WHITE-BOX SOURCE-ONLY audit, Flutter/Dart + Kotlin Android app at /workspace/flames-audit-t196 (real repo /tmp/flames-audit-t196). NO emulator, NO adb, NO running app. Every claim must be static with exact file:line. Findings must be labelled "unconfirmed, not dynamically validated", confidence at most "medium".

FIRST: call get_threat_model(target="/workspace/flames-audit-t196") and read it.

YOUR JOB: adversarially re-derive (do NOT take my word for it) and then either BREAK or CONFIRM the following candidate. Your default stance must be falsification: hunt for a control that blocks it.

CANDIDATE: A malicious co-resident Android app with NO permissions sends an Intent (ACTION_SEND, type text/plain, EXTRA_TEXT="<attacker text>", explicit ComponentName ai.hermes.flames/.MainActivity — note explicit intents need no intent-filter match) to the exported, non-permission-guarded MainActivity. The shared text is then auto-submitted to the on-device LLM agent as a user turn with NO user confirmation, and if it contains an http(s) URL the app auto-fetches that URL (unvalidated host — loopback/private ranges allowed) before submitting.

Chain to independently verify or break (re-derive every hop yourself; do not trust these line numbers, they may be off by a few):
1. android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml — MainActivity exported=true, not permission-guarded, declares ACTION_SEND / SEND_MULTIPLE filters (text/*, image/*, */*).
2. Plugin receive_sharing_intent 1.9.0 (pubspec.yaml, pubspec.lock) — its Kotlin source is extracted at /tmp/rsi. Verify it reads EXTRA_TEXT and emits it as the JSON "path" field, and that onAttachedToActivity (initial intent) and onNewIntent (live intent) both feed the Dart stream/method channel.
3. Dart: lib/domain/services/share/share_target_service.dart, lib/presentation/screen/share/cubit/share_target_cubit.dart, lib/domain/entities/share/shared_payload.dart.
4. lib/presentation/screen/chat/chat_screen.dart — the share-cubit subscription in initState and _submitSharedPayloads; then _handleSubmitted.
5. lib/presentation/screen/chat/cubit/agent_cubit.dart sendMessage -> ReAct loop, and the tool tier gate (lib/domain/tools/chat/security_policy.dart, tool_registry.dart executeTool).
6. lib/domain/tools/chat/url_reader_service.dart (validateUrl) and lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/url_reader_service.dart (Dio GET, followRedirects).

SPECIFICALLY TRY TO BREAK IT — check each and report the result explicitly:
(a) Is there ANY confirmation dialog, user tap, settings toggle, feature flag, or consent gate anywhere between the incoming intent and sendMessage? Grep the whole repo, including settings keys and any "share" preference.
(b) Is ChatScreen actually mounted in production (cold start via the share intent)? Trace lib/myapp.dart bootstrap -> app_router.dart initialLocation -> splash_screen.dart navigation -> main_navigation_shell.dart IndexedStack. Does the share cubit get initialised on cold start, and is the cold-start payload drained?
(c) Does the plugin's Kotlin really reach the Dart layer for a cold start (getInitialMedia) AND for a warm start (onNewIntent), or is one path dead (e.g. FlutterActivity not forwarding onNewIntent, launchMode singleTop, missing plugin registration)?
(d) Does `_submitSharedPayloads` really run BEFORE any user action, or is it gated by `mounted`, by an empty-payload check, or by a mode check that fails in practice?
(e) Does the URL fetch actually happen before submission, and does validateUrl really permit http://127.0.0.1/, http://192.168.1.1/, http://169.254.169.254/ (read the exact code)? Does Dio on Flutter (dart:io sockets) honour Android's cleartext block? Check pubspec.yaml/pubspec.lock for any Dio adapter override (e.g. native_dio_adapter, cronet) and check lib/common/injection/modules.dart for the Dio singleton definition.
(f) Is there anything that marks the shared text as untrusted before it becomes a user turn (e.g. a "[LINK CONTEXT]" provenance marker, or wrapping)? Note exactly what you find — the link-context marker exists but check WHERE it is applied and whether the raw attacker text is also present unmarked.
(g) Could an unprivileged app really not achieve the same thing another way (i.e. is this a non-issue because "any app can do this anyway")? Assess honestly: consider an app WITHOUT the INTERNET permission, and consider attribution.

IF THE CHAIN HOLDS (no blocking control found): file exactly ONE create_vulnerability_report. Requirements:
- Focus the headline on the strongest defensible claim: an unverified third-party Intent channel auto-triggers a full agent turn (LLM call + on-device ReAct tool loop) with no user confirmation. Mention the attacker-chosen outbound fetch (loopback/private-range reachable, response body injected into the LLM context) as a secondary aspect, honestly rated — do NOT call it high.
- target: the repository path. endpoint: the Android component (ai.hermes.flames/.MainActivity). method: null.
- cwe: choose between CWE-940 (Improper Verification of Source of a Communication Channel) and CWE-862 (Missing Authorization) — pick the most defensible and justify it in one line inside technical_analysis.
- cvss_breakdown: be honest and conservative. Suggested vector to sanity-check (adjust if your trace disagrees): AV:L, AC:L, PR:N, UI:N, S:U, C:N, I:L, A:N (a malicious local app is required; the deterministic consequences are an unauthorized agent turn plus an attacker-chosen outbound request; tool-invocation consequences depend on model compliance and are NOT demonstrated). Do not inflate.
- confidence: "medium" and confidence_rationale naming the proof gap (static-only, no emulator/adb, no runtime reproduction).
- counterevidence: required — state what you actively checked and found, and any constraint that limits it.
- severity_change_conditions: required.
- code_locations: REQUIRED. Provide a minimal repository-native Dart fix in lib/presentation/screen/chat/chat_screen.dart that removes the auto-submission: stage the shared prompt into the composer for the user to review and send explicitly, instead of calling _handleSubmitted. fix_before must be a VERBATIM copy of the exact current lines (read the file; verify line numbers), fix_after the complete replacement. Check what toast/notification helper actually exists in the repo before using one (do not invent an API). Also state in remediation_steps (prose, no code) that the intent source should be treated as untrusted input.
- fix_verification: REQUIRED and must be honest — say which gates you could only reason about because there is no runtime (no emulator/adb, cannot run flutter test for a widget-level proof; state whether `flutter analyze`/`dart analyze` is even runnable in this sandbox and what happened if you tried). Do not claim a gate passed that you did not execute.
- fix_pr_body: markdown PR body.

Also call record_coverage for: surface "ai.hermes.flames/.MainActivity SEND intent", risk_area "share-intent auto-submit to agent (CWE-940)" and surface "shared-URL auto-fetch", risk_area "SSRF / attacker-chosen outbound request" — with the correct outcome (reported / ruled_out with the named control at file:line / needs_follow_up).

Then agent_finish with: confirmed or not, exact file:line of every hop, report id if filed, and open_items.

WHITE-BOX SOURCE-ONLY audit of the Flames Android Flutter app at /workspace/flames-audit-t196 (real repo /tmp/flames-audit-t196, mounted read-write).

FIRST: call get_threat_model(target="/workspace/flames-audit-t196") and read it — shared baseline. Record coverage with record_coverage as you go.

YOUR MISSION — **the Android IPC / intent attack surface**, i.e. what a malicious co-resident third-party app can do to Flames.

FILES YOU OWN:
- android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
- android/app/src/main/kotlin/ai/hermes/flames/*.kt (all 8 files, especially MainActivity.kt, RationaleActivity.kt, FlamesNotificationListenerService.kt, FlamesAccessibilityService.kt, FlamesQuickTile.kt, FlamesBackgroundService.kt, FlamesOverlayBubble.kt)
- lib/presentation/screen/share/ + its cubit
- lib/domain/services/share/ and lib/domain/entities/share/
- the Dart-side intent / deep-link / platform-channel handling (search for MethodChannel, EventChannel, onNewIntent, getInitialLink, receive_sharing_intent or similar plugin usage)

REQUIRED ANALYSIS (exact file:line per claim):
1. Enumerate EVERY exported component from the manifest and classify each: exported-because-permission-guarded (BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE / BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE / BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE / START_VIEW_PERMISSION_USAGE) vs exported-and-reachable-by-any-third-party-app. `MainActivity` and `RationaleActivity` are NOT permission-guarded — that is the interesting pair. State precisely what a malicious app can achieve by starting each one with crafted extras / data URI / flags.
2. MainActivity's `SEND` / `SEND_MULTIPLE` / `VIEW content://` (BROWSABLE) filters: trace where `EXTRA_TEXT`, `EXTRA_STREAM`, and `content://` URIs are consumed. Is the URI scheme validated? Is the path validated? Can a `file://` or a crafted `content://` provider URI cause arbitrary file read, path traversal, or an upload of a file outside the intended scope? Can `EXTRA_TEXT` be crafted into a prompt-injection / auto-execute path (does a shared item auto-send to the agent or auto-invoke a tool)?
3. Intent redirection: does any exported component take a nested Intent / PendingIntent / component name from extras and forward it (the classic "intent redirection" pattern)? Search the Kotlin for `getParcelableExtra`, `Intent.parseUri`, `setComponent`, `startActivity` with an attacker-influenced Intent.
4. `RationaleActivity` (Health Connect rationale, exported, unguarded): what does it do, and can it be used for anything beyond displaying a rationale (e.g. deep-linking into privileged actions, leaking state, being used as an intent-redirect trampoline)?
5. `FlamesNotificationListenerService`: confirm the permission gate actually applies, and check whether the service exposes any additional public binder method or static state that another app could reach.
6. `FlamesAccessibilityService`: same — is the service's data accessible to other components of the app / other apps? Check accessibility_service_config.xml for `canRetrieveWindowContent` and any `android:settingsActivity` that is exported.
7. `android:allowBackup` is NOT declared (Android default = true) and there is no `fullBackupContent`/`dataExtractionRules`. Determine exactly which app-private files would be included in an ADB/cloud backup given the app's storage layout (find the storage paths in lib/). Assess honestly and state the consequence.
8. Also: no `network_security_config` and no `usesCleartextTraffic` — search the Dart and Kotlin for any `http://` URL literal or cleartext socket and state whether any code path would actually fail or silently downgrade.

DELIVERABLE:
- For each CONCRETE candidate, spawn a focused child agent to independently validate and, if it holds, file with create_vulnerability_report including the inline fix (code_locations with verbatim fix_before/fix_after + fix_verification + fix_pr_body). NO dynamic validation is possible (no emulator/adb) — confidence at most "medium" and the report must state "unconfirmed, not dynamically validated". Android-manifest findings should cite the manifest line and the Dart/Kotlin consumer line.
- Candidates that do NOT hold: name the specific control (file:line) → record_coverage(outcome="ruled_out"). Cannot name one → outcome="needs_follow_up". Never silently drop.
- agent_finish with summary + open_items.

Note: Android 12+ requires `android:exported` explicitly, and components with a system `BIND_*` permission are NOT reachable by third-party apps — do not over-report those. Precision matters more than volume.

agents.agent_name: Arbitrary File Read Via Device File Tools
agents.task:
WHITE-BOX SOURCE-ONLY audit of the Flames Android Flutter app at /workspace/flames-audit-t196. NO emulator, NO adb, NO running app — you CANNOT execute anything. Any report MUST say "unconfirmed, not dynamically validated" and use confidence at most "medium".

FIRST: call get_threat_model(target="/workspace/flames-audit-t196"), and call get_note("0f5014") — the authoritative tool-tier map. Build on it.

YOUR SINGLE FOCUS: **arbitrary file read / unbounded filesystem enumeration via the `read_device_file` and `list_device_files` agent tools.**

The claim to verify (I have already done the primary reading — confirm or refute each point with exact file:line):

1. `lib/domain/tools/chat/tool_registry.dart:762` registers `read_device_file`, described as "Reads a text file from the device workspace", parameter `path` = **"Absolute file path to read"**. Declared `securityTier: SecurityTier.tier2Permission` with `checkPermission: () => service.checkPermission()`.
2. `lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/file_workspace_service.dart:78` — `DefaultFileSystemWrapper.checkPermission() async => true;` and `:81` `requestPermission() async => true;`. So the Tier-2 permission gate at `tool_registry.dart:250-255` ALWAYS PASSES. The declared tier is effectively a no-op.

Note the two backends differ: sqlite_memory_datasource.dart:288-304 catches and falls back to `_searchWithLike`, while the LIVE implementation local_memory_service.dart:313-330 has no such catch, so the throw reaches :334 and returns `Left(StorageFailure('memory_unavailable'))`; agent_cubit.dart:522-526 ignores the Left, leaving `_activeMemories` stale rather than cleared. Severity low/informational — carried in open_items rather than filed as a vulnerability.

entries.surface: agent_cubit ReAct message construction (agent_cubit.dart:906-921) + memory re-injection (:907-914) + session hydration (:272-273)
entries.risk_area: Persistent prompt injection (untrusted content re-injected across turns via memory vault and session history)
entries.evidence: Resolved by two filed reports that together cover both persistence paths. (1) The unframed tool-result channel is filed as vuln-0004 ("Screen text read from any app is injected into the agent prompt as a tool result with no untrusted-data framing", high, CVSS 8.1) — root cause: untrusted tool-result text enters the prompt with no data/instruction framing, evidenced on the accessibility channel; its remediation explicitly carries notification/web-page/memory as the same open class. (2) The memory re-injection path is carried as impact in vuln-0005 ("Tools with device-state side effects are classified Tier 1 ... and auto-execute with no authorization gate") — `save_memory` is tier1Auto so the write needs no approval, and agent_cubit.dart:907-914 re-injects `_activeMemories` as a `role:'system'` message every turn. The Tier-1 validator also independently verified the SQLite persistence (flames_memory.db). No separate report needed — filing a third one would fragment one root cause.
entries.recorded_by: Tool Tier Gate And Prompt Injection

entries.risk_area: Unauthorized sensitive-data collection / permission bypass
entries.evidence: Read is gated in Dart code, not just the manifest: health_service.dart:195-203 resolves HealthMetrics.permissionByMetric[metric] and rejects with 'health_permission_denied' unless grantedPermissions.contains(permission), immediately before _platform.readMetric at :205. The native side re-checks: FlamesHealthConnect.kt:75 returns null when permissionFor(metric) is null and Health Connect's own permissionController enforces the grant (health_service.dart:196-203 reads grantedPermissions from it). Tool is tier2Permission with checkPermission: () => service.checkPermission() (tool_registry.dart:1704-1705), and checkPermission (health_service.dart:243-260) returns false unless a supported metric's permission is actually granted. No health data is read by default or pushed continuously; the read is explicit-call-only. Data goes to the user's configured LLM as a tool result like any other tool. No hardcoded alternate endpoint.

entries.surface: Device sensor tools: location, camera (built-in + external UVC), contacts, NFC, clipboard
entries.risk_area: Unauthorized sensitive-data collection and exfiltration to an unexpected endpoint
entries.evidence: Location: tool is tier2Permission with checkPermission: () => locationService.checkPermission() (tool_registry.dart:317). location_service.dart:26-34 checks isLocationServiceEnabled() then geolocator.checkPermission() and returns false unless whileInUse/always; getLocation re-checks at :62-75 before any position read. Camera: camera_take_photo is tier2Permission (tool_registry.dart:372); external_camera_capture is tier2Permission with checkPermission: () => service.isCameraPermissionGranted() (tool_registry.dart:446) and its own USB-permission check (tool_registry.dart:474-497). Frames/preview are rendered to a Flutter texture (external_camera_preview_cubit.dart:118-162) — no network code exists in external_camera_service.dart (grep for http/url/socket/upload returns nothing); a captured frame only leaves the device when the model receives it as a tool result from the user's own configured LLM. Contacts: checkPermission at tool_registry.dart:1366. NFC: nfc_read_tag and nfc_read_emoney_balance are tier2Permission (tool_registry.dart:1568, 1621) with device NFC-enabled checks. Clipboard: clipboard_read/clipboard_write are tier1Auto (tool_registry.dart:273, 291) — read of the user's own clipboard to the user's own configured server, no third party involved. No hardcoded or config-driven alternate endpoint exists for any of these: the only outbound destinations in the app are the user-configured LLM base URL and gateway URL.

entries.risk_area: Continuous/background sensitive-data collection
entries.evidence: FlamesBackgroundService.kt:167-262 handles only intent actions START_SERVICE/STOP_SERVICE/UPDATE_NOTIFICATION/VOICE_INPUT/CANCEL_VOICE/SHOW_BUBBLE/HIDE_BUBBLE. It never touches FlamesAccessibilityService, never reads Health Connect, and never reads the notification buffer; its only cross-process call is channel.invokeMethod("onActionReceived", <token>) to the Dart side (lines 226, 248, 276). It holds a bounded PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK (FlamesBackgroundService.kt:103-121, clamped 1s-60s). So there is no continuous or background collection of accessibility or health data: the accessibility tree is pull-only via getScreenTree (MainActivity.kt:186-190) and the health read is explicit-call-only. Notification buffer is in-memory, capped, and populated only by the separate notification listener service.

entries.risk_area: SQL injection via FTS5 MATCH query building
entries.evidence: LocalMemoryService / SqliteMemoryDatasource build the FTS5 MATCH query as a parameter, not by interpolation: sqlite_memory_datasource.dart:290-300 uses 'WHERE memories_fts MATCH ?' with whereArgs [sanitizedMatchQuery, limit]; the query is first reduced to word characters by _extractWords (:445-454, regex strips non-word chars) and _sanitizeFtsQuery (:456-461) emits only 'word* OR word*'. All other statements use where/whereArgs binding (e.g. :210-215, :228-237, :346-350). LIKE fallback also parameterized (:324-340). No injection sink found. Note: whether stored memory content is treated as trusted when replayed into the prompt is a SEPARATE candidate under review by another agent (memory → role:system injection) — not closed by this entry.

entries.risk_area: Prompt injection via attacker-controlled notification text
entries.evidence: Resolved and filed as vuln-0010 ("Notification text from any installed app reaches the agent prompt with no data/instruction separation and can drive auto-executing Tier-1 device tools", medium, CVSS 4.2, confidence medium). Hop-by-hop trace verified by reading every file: FlamesNotificationListenerService.kt:62-73 copies EXTRA_TITLE/EXTRA_TEXT verbatim with no length cap and no self-package exclusion → MainActivity.kt:124-128 → notification_triage_service.dart:264-274 (plain jsonEncode, no envelope) → tool_registry.dart:821/:851 → agent_cubit.dart:820-825 → :906/:917-921 → chat_message.dart:116-127 (no transformation). Absence of any control proven by exhaustive search; the app's own SkillSecurityScanner has exactly one production caller (skill_import_service.dart:44) and never sees notification text.
entries.recorded_by: Tool Tier Gate And Prompt Injection

entries.risk_area: Unauthorized health-data read via an agent tool
entries.evidence: get_health_data (tool_registry.dart:1680) is Tier 2 WITH `checkPermission: () => service.checkPermission()` (:1705) — the gate at tool_registry.dart:250-255 actually runs. health_status (:1665) is Tier 1 but is a pure availability/permission-report read (no metric data). Health Connect data is thus correctly gated; no bypass found.
entries.recorded_by: Tool Tier Gate And Prompt Injection

entries.surface: Outbound endpoint inventory + logging of sensitive values (whole app)
entries.risk_area: Data egress to an unexpected/hardcoded third-party endpoint; sensitive data in logs
entries.evidence: Exhaustive grep for analytics/telemetry/crash SDKs in pubspec.yaml, lib/ and android/app/build.gradle.kts found no Firebase, Crashlytics, Sentry, Amplitude or Mixpanel dependency. The only outbound destinations are: (1) the user-configured LLM base URL (agent_cubit.dart:121 default 'https://api.openai.com/v1', overridable per server profile), (2) the user-configured Hermes gateway URL (gateway_client.dart:149-151 scheme handling), (3) hardcoded GitHub release URLs for Piper TTS voice models (lib/domain/entities/chat/piper_voice.dart:37,48,59), and (4) a wa.me deep link built for the user to tap (contact_launcher_tools.dart:128-130). Device data (health/location/screen/camera/notifications) is never sent to (3) or (4). Note the local_memory_service.dart:282,335,474 developer.log calls emit only the string 'memory_unavailable' plus a truncated DB error reason — no memory content, no key, no secret. No log/print/debug path emits an API key, bearer token, or Authorization header.

entries.surface: ToolRegistry tier gate (SecurityTier enforcement) vs remote skill/gateway/model input
entries.risk_area: Tool tier downgrade from remote/untrusted input (HITL bypass)
entries.evidence: Tier gating is decided purely by local constants: securityTier is set literally at each RegisteredTool definition in tool_registry.dart and SecurityPolicy (security_policy.dart:6-29) maps it to auto/permission/HITL. The gate is evaluated in Dart before execute: agent_cubit.dart:750-757 pauses on tier3Hitl and emits WaitingApproval; tool_registry.dart:250-253 re-checks checkPermission for tier2. The gateway RPC path (gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:143-148) also consults the registry, and its approval callback is requested per call (lines 110-140). I found no code path where a remote skill package, a tool result, a gateway frame, or model output writes to a tool's securityTier. Skill packages carry a free-text 'tier' YAML field (skills_registry_service.dart:50) but it is only a display string on the Skill entity — confirm it is not read by the tier gate. Residual: tier2 tools registered with a null checkPermission (ui_find_elements, read_web_page, nfc_read_tag, nfc_read_emoney_balance) execute with no registry permission check by design — that is a per-tool property, not a remote downgrade, and is covered by the individual tool entries.

entries.surface: lib/domain/tools/chat/tool_registry.dart — Tier-1 "Read-Only / Ambient" classification of side-effecting tools
entries.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / security-tier misclassification (ungated device side effects)
entries.evidence: Independently re-verified and filed as vuln-0005. Contract: security_policy.dart:3 "Tier 1: Read-Only / Ambient (auto-execute)"; :17-19 isAutoExecute returns true only for tier1Auto and is referenced NOWHERE else in the repository (dead predicate). Single gate: agent_cubit.dart:753 is the only branch that pauses (`== SecurityTier.tier3Hitl` → WaitingApproval + return at :761); Tier 1/2 fall through to executeTool at :766. Registry gate tool_registry.dart:250-256 has no Tier-1 branch. Six side-effecting tools confirmed at tier1Auto with NO checkPermission in their blocks (verified by per-block grep): clipboard_write :279/:291, send_local_notification :692/:708, save_memory :884/:899, delete_memory :921/:930, register_geofence :953/:968, manage_background_service :1168/:1213. Smoking gun: send_local_notification (tier1Auto) and schedule_reminder (tier3Hitl :742) are registered by the SAME method registerNotificationTools(NotificationServiceBase service) at :689 against the same service instance; data/.../notification_service.dart:74-86 shows the Tier-1 path calling _plugin.show() immediately. Third independent inconsistency: bundled skill notification_reminders (skills_registry_service.dart:561-574) declares these tools with tier 'Tier 2 Perm', and Skill.isEnabled defaults true (skill.dart:29). Repository's own tests exercise these ungated: e2e_fase3_intelligence_test.dart:281-296 (save_memory), :560-580 (register_geofence), e2e_fase4_voice_test.dart:303-319 (manage_background_service). Second caller gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:89/:148 gates only Tier 3. Tools enabled by default (tool_registry.dart:210, :222).

entries.surface: agent_cubit.dart memory re-injection as system-role message (persistence amplifier for save_memory)
entries.risk_area: Persistent prompt injection / instruction-data confusion
entries.evidence: Covered as the persistence-amplifier impact of vuln-0005, with the untrusted-data delimiter fix included inline in that report. Verified: agent_cubit.dart:907-914 builds memoryPrompt by string interpolation of m.key/m.content with no delimiter and inserts it as role:'system' at position 0; block sits inside _runLoop (declared :864) which recurses at :831, so it is rebuilt every turn; _activeMemories populated at :519-527 via searchMemories(prompt.trim(), 3). Write path: save_memory :884/:899 (tier1Auto) → local_memory_service.dart:498 → sqlite_memory_datasource.dart:190 inserts into table `memories` of the on-disk DB `flames_memory.db` (:16), so content survives app restart. Destruction path: delete_memory :921/:930 → local_memory_service.dart:570 → sqlite_memory_datasource.dart:343/:357 db.delete('memories', ...) with no confirmation. Honest limit: retrieval is FTS-driven (agent_cubit.dart:519-527), so injected content must match later prompt vocabulary to resurface — narrowed foothold, not removed. Residual gap unchanged: LLM compliance was never executed (no emulator/adb), so this remains unconfirmed, not dynamically validated.

entries.risk_area: Skill tool-disable policy bypass via tool_search/tool_describe re-discovery
entries.evidence: agent_cubit.dart:896-905 re-adds tools discovered via `tool_search`/`tool_describe` to the model's tool list, but line 897 `if (!_toolRegistry.isToolEnabled(name)) continue;` re-checks the enabled state before each re-add. Combined with executeTool's own `if (!isToolEnabled(name)) return Left(...)` at tool_registry.dart:246-248, a skill-disabled tool cannot be re-enabled or executed through the discovery meta-tools. The `tool_search` result parser (:800-816) also only records names that exist in the registry.

entries.risk_area: Secrets at rest in plaintext (API key, gateway token, server profiles)
entries.evidence: FlutterSecureStorage is constructed with default AndroidOptions (lib/common/injection/modules.dart:23; lib/data/datasources/local/settings/secure_storage_service.dart:56-57). In flutter_secure_storage 9.2.4 the Android plugin then encrypts every value with AES-CBC-PKCS7 under an AES key RSA-wrapped by an AndroidKeyStore key (plugin FlutterSecureStorage.java write()/decodeRawValue(); ciphers/StorageCipher18Implementation.java, alias '<pkg>.FlutterSecureStoragePluginKey'); the init-failure fallback at ensureInitialized() still uses that cipher. No code path writes llm_api_key/server_profiles_list anywhere else. Control: plugin AES cipher at write() before editor.putString.

entries.risk_area: Exported Android component reachability / permission gate classification
entries.evidence: Manifest: all android:exported=true components classified. Permission-guarded (NOT third-party reachable): FlamesNotificationListenerService (BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE, manifest:123-131), FlamesAccessibilityService (BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE, manifest:133-144), FlamesQuickTile (BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE, manifest:146-155), ViewPermissionUsageActivity alias (START_VIEW_PERMISSION_USAGE, manifest:174-183). Unguarded: MainActivity (manifest:57-116) and RationaleActivity (manifest:166-172). FlamesBackgroundService exported=false (manifest:157-164). No caller-identity checks anywhere in android/ (rg for getCallingActivity/getCallingPackage/Binder.getCallingUid = 0 hits). All plugin manifests in the dependency tree checked (image_picker, url_launcher, geolocator, flutter_local_notifications, third_party/contacts_service) - no additional exported components. MainActivity action-extra injection candidate handed to child agent 66745bb5 for validation.

entries.risk_area: IPC / binder exposure
entries.evidence: FlamesBackgroundService.kt:165 `override fun onBind(intent: Intent?): IBinder? = null` - no binder exposed. No exported=true on the service (manifest:157-164). All ACTION_* intents are dispatched only from MainActivity (in-process) or the QS tile; third-party apps cannot start an exported=false service. No getStringExtra from external intents reaches onStartCommand.

entries.surface: Every print/debugPrint/developer.log site in lib/ (6 call sites)
entries.risk_area: Secrets in application logs (logcat / developer.log / debugPrint)
entries.evidence: All log sinks in lib/ enumerated by ripgrep: local_memory_service.dart:282,335,474 (logs only a <=160-char DatabaseException cause via _shortReason, :657-663), gateway_client.dart:497 (logs close cause/code/reason/state — the reason is the socket error text, never the auth frame), gateway_link_cubit.dart:194 (state names and durations only), failure_message.dart:18 (logs the exception), myapp.dart:38,49,59,69 (init failure text). No site interpolates apiKey/token/profile/baseUrl. Control: no credential value flows into any of these six log call sites (verified by reading each call site and the objects it prints).

entries.risk_area: Intent redirection / state leakage via exported activity
entries.evidence: RationaleActivity.kt:7-17 takes NO input from the launching intent (no getStringExtra, no getData, no nested Intent), unconditionally starts a hardcoded `androidx.health.ACTION_HEALTH_CONNECT_SETTINGS` intent, then finishes. It cannot be used as an intent-redirect trampoline (target is a constant), leaks no state, and grants no privileged action beyond opening Health Connect settings (which any app can already do via that public action). The only oddity is that it is exported without the START_VIEW_PERMISSION_USAGE permission that the ViewPermissionUsageActivity alias uses - a hygiene issue, not a reachable vulnerability, because the activity itself has no attacker-influenced behaviour.

entries.surface: android:allowBackup default (unset) and app storage layout
entries.risk_area: Data-at-rest / backup exposure
entries.evidence: Reviewed and handed to the scan's reporting flow: no android:allowBackup / fullBackupContent / dataExtractionRules anywhere in android/ (rg = 0 hits), so Android's allowBackup=true default applies. App-private plaintext stores captured by ADB/cloud backup: databases/flames_chat.db (chat_local_datasource.dart:26), databases/flames_memory.db (sqlite_memory_datasource.dart:16), databases/flames_skills.db (skills_local_datasource.dart:15), Hive box `action_center` (action_center_datasource.dart:23,32), and files/ documents (file_workspace_service.dart:66). Secrets are NOT in these stores (llm_api_key/gateway token go to FlutterSecureStorage, secure_storage_service.dart:41-42,67-73; modules.dart:23). Filed by the Baseline SAST agent as vuln-0002 (low, CVSS 3.7, CWE-312).

entries.surface: SecurityTier resolution for registered tools (tool_registry.dart / security_policy.dart)
entries.risk_area: Tool tier downgrade from remote/untrusted input
entries.evidence: Tool tier is a local `const` set at each `register(...)` call (e.g. tool_registry.dart:267, 279, 692, 821, 851) from the `SecurityTier` enum at security_policy.dart:6-10. No remote input reaches the tier: gateway RPC frames (gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:72-89) read `tool.securityTier` from the same registry object; skill frontmatter `tier` is never consulted by any gate (skill_security_scanner.dart:189-190 states it is display-only); tool arguments cannot set a tier. No downgrade path found.

entries.risk_area: Release build integrity / signing configuration
entries.evidence: Confirmed the release build type sets signingConfig = signingConfigs.getByName("debug"), no signingConfigs block exists, and no key.properties / .jks / .keystore is present anywhere in the repository (the Android .gitignore already lists them, showing a release keystore was intended). Also confirmed isMinifyEnabled and isShrinkResources are unset for release. Filed as vuln-0001 with an inline fix.

entries.risk_area: Cleartext transport / network security config
entries.evidence: RESOLVED — the runtime question is answered, and the answer is that cleartext is NOT blocked. This entry's open gap ("the decisive fact could not be resolved statically") is now closed with authoritative sources at the exact Flutter revision this repo pins (.metadata, Flutter 3.47.4): (1) dart:io invokes an embedder hook before every connection — `void Function(Uri) _httpConnectionHook = (_) {};` (sdk/lib/_http/embedder_config.dart), called from `_openUrl` in http_impl.dart; the default allows everything. (2) Flutter installs its own gate `_getHttpConnectionHookClosure(bool mayInsecurelyConnectToAllDomains)` (engine lib/ui/hooks.dart), which permits a connection when that flag is true OR the scheme is https, and otherwise throws. (3) The flag defaults to permissive — `bool may_insecurely_connect_to_all_domains = true;` (engine common/settings.h) — and is only cleared by the `--disallow-insecure-connections` switch (shell/common/switches.cc). (4) The Android embedding at this revision never passes that switch, and forwards an empty domain network policy; the former opt-in manifest mechanism (`io.flutter.network-policy`) was removed upstream and this app declares no such metadata. Therefore http:// and ws:// are fully functional on every supported API level, and `android:usesCleartextTraffic` / a network security config would not govern this path at all (it is enforced by the Java/OkHttp stack, which this app does not use for API traffic). The credential-exposure consequence is filed as vuln-0009 (now medium, CVSS 5.9). Note the earlier "no_issue_found" was wrong on the premise, not just incomplete.

entries.risk_area: Intent redirection / confused deputy
entries.evidence: No nested Intent / PendingIntent / component-name extras are read from any exported component's incoming intent. rg for getParcelableExtra|Intent.parseUri|setComponent|setClassName across android/ returns only the receive_sharing_intent plugin's own EXTRA_STREAM Uri parsing (plugin source, /tmp/rsi, ReceiveSharingIntentPlugin.kt:121,127 - handled by the separate path-traversal child). MainActivity only reads `extra_flames_action` (String) and passes it through the background channel (covered by the action-injection child). No startActivity is called with an attacker-supplied Intent; all startActivity targets are hardcoded Settings.* actions or an explicit component.

entries.risk_area: Sensitive data at rest / platform backup exposure
entries.evidence: Confirmed no android:allowBackup, dataExtractionRules or fullBackupContent attribute exists anywhere in android/, and no backup rules resource exists under res/xml/. Traced the plaintext stores that fall inside the default backup include set: flames_chat.db, flames_memory.db, flames_skills.db and the Hive action_center box. Credentials are separately held in FlutterSecureStorage so are not directly exposed. Filed as vuln-0002 with an inline fix.

entries.risk_area: Known-CVE dependency / supply chain
entries.evidence: OSV API queried directly (bypassing the sandbox proxy, which was blocking api.osv.dev) for all 247 pinned Pub packages in pubspec.lock, using exact resolved versions. Zero vulnerabilities returned. Verified the query path works with two positive controls: lodash@4.17.4 returned 10 advisories and archive@3.3.0 returned 2 (GHSA-9v85-q87q-g4vg, GHSA-r285-q736-9v95). entries.surface: Tier-3 HITL approval gate (agent_cubit.dart:756-761, :611-613) and approval UI (action_approval_sheet.dart:44-45)
entries.risk_area: HITL approval bypass / argument mutation between approval and execution
entries.evidence: agent_cubit.dart:760-761 pauses on `registered.securityTier == SecurityTier.tier3Hitl` and emits WaitingApproval; approveAction at :611-613 executes the SAME `pending.parameters` object that was stored at :756-759 — no re-derivation, no mutation between approval and execution. action_approval_sheet.dart:44-45 renders `JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ').convert(request.parameters)`, i.e. the real arguments, not a model-controlled summary. No TOCTOU / summary-spoofing bypass found.

entries.surface: ToolRegistry.executeTool permission gate (tool_registry.dart:238-257) for Tier-2 tools without checkPermission
entries.risk_area: Missing permission evaluation on tier2Permission tools (tier enforcement gap)
entries.evidence: Resolved and filed as vuln-0006 ("Tier-2 permission gate fails open for tools registered without a permission checker", medium, CVSS 4.3, CWE-863, confidence medium). The gate is `requiresPermission(tier) && tool.checkPermission != null` (tool_registry.dart:250-256), so a Tier-2 tool with a null checker skips permission evaluation entirely; `checkPermission` is an optional constructor param (:51,:59) so nothing prevents the omission. Six registrations confirmed without a checker (camera_take_photo, open_external_url, open_email_composer, launch_system_setting, nfc_read_tag, nfc_read_emoney_balance); a seventh (ui_find_elements) is a documented deliberate omission whose service self-checks and was ruled out. Contrast case confirmed load-bearing: 8 Tier-2 tools DO pass runtime-permission checkers. Tier is a local const and not attacker-influenceable.

entries.surface: android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml application element + shared_prefs credential store
entries.risk_area: Secret exposure via Android backup (allowBackup default / cloud + adb backup)
entries.evidence: android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml declares no android:allowBackup (defaults true) and no fullBackupContent/dataExtractionRules; there is no res/xml/backup rules file (only accessibility_service_config.xml). Control: the only credential at-rest ciphertext is written through flutter_secure_storage, whose AES data key is RSA-wrapped by a key in the AndroidKeyStore (plugin FlutterSecureStorage.java write()/decodeRawValue() + StorageCipher18Implementation.java, alias '<pkg>.FlutterSecureStoragePluginKey'); AndroidKeyStore keys are device-bound and are not included in Auto Backup, so a restored copy of shared_prefs/FlutterSecureStorage cannot be decrypted off-device.

entries.surface: All Hive / SharedPreferences / SQLite / file-write sites in lib/
entries.risk_area: Secrets stored outside secure storage (Hive box, SQLite table, plain file)
entries.evidence: Every write of llm_api_key / server_profiles_list goes through SecureStorageService (secure_storage_service.dart:67-69, 189-193); the Hive 'action_center' box stores only ambient battery/geofence ActionItems (action_center_datasource.dart:32,56; ambient_trigger_service.dart:175-192) and chat_local_datasource.dart:118 puts chat history into FlutterSecureStorage, not SQLite; the memory vault, skills store and chat-session SQLite tables hold user content only. No credential value reaches Hive/SQLite/plain files.

entries.risk_area: Plaintext-at-rest exposure of chat message content (API keys pasted by user, tool results with personal data)

No plaintext Hive box holds messages. Residual gap (not this row's risk): session titles and ids go to the unencrypted SQLite DB at :157-179/:201-221, which stores only titles, not message bodies.

entries.risk_area: Unencrypted local storage of action-center inbox records
entries.evidence: Box is opened with no encryption: lib/data/datasources/local/action_center/action_center_datasource.dart:31-34 `Hive.openBox<String>(boxName)` with no HiveAesCipher, rooted at the app documents dir via lib/myapp.dart:45-51 `Hive.initFlutter('flames')`. entries.risk_area: Autonomous/scheduled action execution bypassing the HITL approval gate
entries.evidence: Named controls: (a) ActionCenterCubit.executeAction (lib/presentation/screen/action_center/cubit/action_center_cubit.dart:63-72) only calls markAsRead and sets lastExecutedActionId — it performs no tool invocation, navigation, or platform call; (b) the payload's only consumed field is a display label (lib/presentation/screen/action_center/widgets/action_item_card.dart:62-63), and an `open_settings` key is explicitly treated as an inert navigation marker (:65, :69-71); (c) the sole producers are the local battery reader and local geofence engine (ambient_trigger_service.dart:216-349) — no gateway frame, model tool call, or notification can create an item, and grep shows no other ActionItem construction site. Nothing here crosses the HITL boundary because no action executes at all. The ambient WorkManager callback (ambient_trigger_service.dart:16-19) returns true without performing work, and no receiver is declared for RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED (AndroidManifest.xml:10 only requests the permission), so nothing runs at boot.

entries.risk_area: Missing authorization / IPC action injection (CWE-862)
entries.evidence: Confirmed by full source trace and filed as vuln-0003. Chain: exported unguarded MainActivity (AndroidManifest.xml:57-76, no android:permission) -> extractActionFromIntent reads attacker-controlled extra with no allowlist (MainActivity.kt:73-85) -> onNewIntent forwards over method channel (MainActivity.kt:59-66) -> Dart switch with no validation (voice_turn_action_listener.dart:162-178) -> VoiceTurnService.runTurn -> VoiceInputService.startListening -> speech recognizer opens mic (voice_turn_service.dart:141, voice_input_service.dart:202). Repo-wide rg for getCallingActivity/getCallingPackage/getCallingUid/checkCallingPermission/getReferrer returned zero matches. No user confirmation or lifecycle gate on the mic path. Static-only, no device/emulator, confidence medium.

entries.surface: RationaleActivity (exported, no permission) — intent redirection / privileged action trampoline
entries.risk_area: Intent redirection, exported-component abuse
entries.evidence: RationaleActivity.kt:7-17 has no attacker-controlled input path: onCreate takes no extras, reads no data URI, and the only action it performs is startActivity(Intent("androidx.health.ACTION_HEALTH_CONNECT_SETTINGS")) with a hardcoded action, then finish(). It cannot be used as an intent-redirect trampoline because it never forwards a caller-supplied Intent, component name, or extras — the outgoing intent is fully literal, and any caller-injected extras on the incoming intent are never read or re-attached. No state is leaked (no output, no result, no logging).

entries.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / Tier-2 permission gate fail-open
entries.evidence: Filed as vuln-0006 (medium, CVSS 4.3): the fail-open Tier-2 gate at `tool_registry.dart:250-256` plus the five silent registrations (`camera_take_photo` :371, `open_external_url` :1432, `open_email_composer` :1493, `launch_system_setting` :1524, `nfc_read_tag` :1568, `nfc_read_emoney_balance` :1621). Confirmed by independent adversarial review (agent 69417682) which could not refute the mechanism: `SecurityPolicy.requiresPermission` is referenced in exactly one place in lib/, `tool.execute` is invoked at exactly one place (:257), and both invocation paths gate only Tier 3. Impact calibrated down to I:L / UI:R because the OS toggle, the mail send button, the OS capture Activity and the physical NFC tap all still stand in the way; report is static-only ("unconfirmed, not dynamically validated"). Fix filed inline: fail-closed gate + explicit `selfEnforcesPermission` marker, with the ui_find_elements and camera_take_photo documented exceptions preserved.

entries.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / remote invocation path bypassing tier gate
entries.evidence: Covered by vuln-0006. `gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:89` gates only `requiresHitl` (tier3) then `:148` calls `toolRegistry.executeTool(request.tool, request.arguments)` with server-supplied name and arguments, so a remote frame reaches the fail-open gate. Independent review confirmed this is one of only three `executeTool` call sites and that no other Tier-2 guard exists. Residual open element: whether an auto-executed `launch_system_setting` navigation to the privilege-granting settings pages chains with the notification-text or skill-package injection surfaces (owned by sibling agents 5ef94689 / 8d54770d) into a higher-impact end-to-end path. Not claimable from this agent's scope; carried in agent_finish open_items.

entries.risk_area: Hardcoded secrets / credentials in source
entries.evidence: Ran gitleaks (2 hits) and trufflehog (3 hits) across the repository. All hits triaged as non-secrets: gitleaks flagged the literal placeholder string sk-valid-key-12345 in docs/TESTCASES.md:33 and test/presentation/screen/settings/cubit/settings_cubit_test.dart:222, which is obviously synthetic test data, not a live credential. trufflehog's 3 URI hits are all inside strix_runs/ scan scaffolding (agents.db), not application code. No hardcoded API key, bearer token or password exists in lib/ or android/.

entries.risk_area: Credential storage location / plaintext fallback
entries.evidence: Confirmed the entire app persists its credentials through FlutterSecureStorage only: SecureStorageService (lib/data/datasources/local/settings/secure_storage_service.dart) wraps FlutterSecureStorage for llm_api_key, llm_base_url, server_profiles_list and related settings, and DI instantiates it with default options at lib/common/injection/modules.dart:23. Searched for a fallback to plaintext stores for credential keys and found none. The plaintext SQLite/Hive stores hold chat content, memory vault rows and Action Center items, not credentials, so this is a storage-hygiene observation rather than a credential-exposure finding. NOTE: the default AndroidOptions of flutter_secure_storage 9.2.4 could not be confirmed from the pub cache (package not downloaded in this environment), so whether Android Keystore-backed encryption is applied by default is unverified - see open items.

entries.risk_area: Unauthorized IPC / service hijack
entries.evidence: The BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE gate at manifest:126 is the platform-enforced control: only the system (or a service the user explicitly enabled in Settings) can bind it, and the OS refuses third-party bind requests to that component. The service exposes no additional binder: it is a plain NotificationListenerService with only companion-object static state (FlamesNotificationListenerService.kt:17-36) reachable solely from MainActivity's own in-process MethodChannel handler (MainActivity.kt:124-135) - a third-party app has no channel to it. The buffer is in-memory only (notificationBuffer, :19).

entries.risk_area: Unauthorized IPC / screen-content exposure
entries.evidence: The BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE gate at manifest:136 is the platform-enforced control (user must enable the service in Settings; third-party bind is refused). The service exposes no binder of its own and no public static accessor that another app can call; its captured tree (FlamesAccessibilityService.kt:51-112) is only reachable through MainActivity's in-process channel (MainActivity.kt:186-190). accessibility_service_config.xml declares android:settingsActivity absent (no exported settings activity) and canRetrieveWindowContent="true" - that is the intended read-only function of the user-enabled service, not a third-party reachable weakness. The service is read-only by design (no performAction calls - verified by rg).

entries.surface: Export, share and clipboard writers in lib/ (file_workspace_service, doc_builder_skill, summary_card, clipboard_service)
entries.risk_area: Secret leakage through export / share / clipboard paths
entries.evidence: No credential is written to any exported location: no share_plus/Share.share usage in lib/ (grep), no settings export/backup function, no debug dump; the only export path is export_document_pdf (doc_builder_skill.dart:75-100) which writes model-provided markdown to the app documents dir. The only Clipboard.setData call is summary_card.dart:36 (chat summary text). No settings/profile object is exposed to agent tools (tool_registry.dart has no settings/clipboard-of-key tool).

entries.surface: android/app/build.gradle.kts, AndroidManifest.xml, flutter_secure_storage 9.2.4 Android plugin defaults
entries.risk_area: Android build/config hygiene affecting credential storage (allowBackup, cleartext, keystore config)
entries.evidence: Only dependency is flutter_secure_storage 9.2.4 (pubspec.lock:544-551). Its Android implementation encrypts values with AES-CBC-PKCS7 under a 16-byte key RSA-wrapped by an AndroidKeyStore key (StorageCipher18Implementation.java + RSACipher18Implementation.java, alias '<pkg>.FlutterSecureStoragePluginKey'), not with AndroidX EncryptedSharedPreferences, because AndroidOptions.encryptedSharedPreferences defaults to false and the app never passes AndroidOptions (modules.dart:23; secure_storage_service.dart:56-57). This is a hardening gap (no GCM integrity, legacy cipher), not a plaintext disclosure: the data key is keystore-wrapped. Android manifest sets no usesCleartextTraffic and no network_security_config.

entries.risk_area: Overlay abuse / tapjacking / agent-state exposure via the floating bubble
entries.evidence: Named controls: (a) the overlay service is declared android:exported="false" (AndroidManifest.xml:157-164), so only this app can start it; (b) FlamesOverlayBubble.show() refuses to add the view unless Settings.canDrawOverlays() is true (FlamesOverlayBubble.kt:38) and the bubble is a bare 56dp ImageView whose only input handler (buildTouchListener, :105-161) calls the app's own onTap callback — it renders no agent state, no text, and exposes no data; (c) tapjacking cannot add authority because the tap only reaches handleBubbleTap (FlamesBackgroundService.kt:268-286), which starts/cancels a voice turn — the same action the user already performs deliberately, and the toggle is symmetric so a spurious tap is not a privilege gain. The bubble is only shown after the user grants SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and enables the setting (overlay_bubble_service.dart:126-154).

entries.risk_area: Credential exposure or third-party control of the background service
entries.evidence: Named control: FlamesBackgroundService is android:exported="false" (AndroidManifest.xml:157-164), so the ACTION_VOICE_INPUT / ACTION_CANCEL_VOICE / ACTION_QUICK_STATUS actions it handles (FlamesBackgroundService.kt:216-259) cannot be delivered by a third-party app. It holds no credentials: the only cross-process state is the MethodChannel reference (dartChannel, :140-153), and the wake lock (:103-134) plus notification text are non-secret. entries.risk_area: Deep link / URI handler triggering a state-changing in-app action
entries.evidence: Named control: the router (lib/presentation/navigation/app_router.dart:26-150) declares only in-app path routes with `state.extra as SomeParams?` casts and no deep-link/URI handler; no uni_links/app_links style plugin is present in pubspec.yaml, and grep finds no getInitialLink/uriLinkStream handler anywhere in lib/. entries.risk_area: Unauthorized IPC / action injection
entries.evidence: BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE (manifest:150) is the platform control - only the system SystemUI may bind; the tile's onClick() (FlamesQuickTile.kt:87-103) starts FlamesBackgroundService with a hardcoded ACTION_VOICE_INPUT. A third-party app cannot bind the tile service, and cannot start the non-exported background service. The tile action itself is an intentional user tap. No extra input is read from the intent.

entries.surface: All Kotlin intent-extra readers (MainActivity, FlamesBackgroundService, FlamesQuickTile, RationaleActivity)
entries.risk_area: Nested Intent / PendingIntent forwarding
entries.evidence: rg for getParcelableExtra/getStringExtra/getData across all android/ Kotlin shows the only externally-influenced reads are MainActivity's `extra_flames_action` (handled by the dedicated candidate/child 66745bb5) and FlamesBackgroundService's EXTRA_TITLE/EXTRA_CONTENT, which are only reachable from MainActivity's in-process MethodChannel and the (non-exported) service's own start paths - no third-party entry point. No android:exported=true receiver or provider exists in the app manifest.

entries.surface: Equatable toString of SettingsState / ServerProfile / GatewayAuthMessage and absence of crash/telemetry reporters
entries.risk_area: Secret exposure through toString()/state serialization into logs or crash reports
entries.evidence: equatable 2.1.0 EquatableConfig.stringify defaults to false (assert-enabled debug only), and GatewayAuthMessage.toString() therefore returns the bare type name; verified by reading the fetched package source (lib/src/equatable.dart:56-61, lib/src/equatable_config.dart). In addition, no BlocObserver/FlutterError.onError/runZonedGuarded handler is installed anywhere in lib/, so state objects carrying apiKey (SettingsState, SettingsData) are never serialized by a framework observer. dio 5.7.0 DioException.toString() prints only type/message/error (no headers, and RequestOptions has no toString override), so the Authorization header cannot reach FailureMessage.humanize's log call at failure_message.dart:18.

entries.risk_area: Secrets or sensitive text written to logcat by native Android code

entries.surface: Flavor and entrypoint configuration (lib/main.dart, pubspec.yaml, android build files)
entries.risk_area: Release configuration hygiene / debug features in production
entries.evidence: Confirmed no String.fromEnvironment, --dart-define, dartDefines or flavor mechanism exists anywhere in lib/ or android/; there is a single entrypoint lib/main.dart with no main_development.dart / main_production.dart split, so no debug-only feature or permissive HTTP client can differ by flavor. entries.surface: Semgrep local-ruleset triage (cleartext + SQL interpolation hits)
entries.risk_area: Cleartext transport / SQL injection in local datastores
entries.evidence: Ran a custom semgrep ruleset (the p/default and p/secrets registry packs were unreachable - semgrep.dev returned HTTP 500 and no cached rules existed). The cleartext rule produced exactly one hit, at lib/data/datasources/remote/settings/server_profile_probe_service_impl.dart:109, which is a ws:// to http:// scheme rewrite inside _normalizeHermesUrl, not a hardcoded cleartext endpoint. Confirmed no network_security_config and no usesCleartextTraffic attribute are declared, so Android 9+ blocks cleartext by default and the app fails closed. Also confirmed the SQL-injection-shaped hits were false positives: every database access uses bound parameters (the FTS MATCH query passes the sanitized term as a ? argument at sqlite_memory_datasource.dart:299, and the LIKE fallback builds only the fixed condition string while values go through whereArgs).

entries.risk_area: Audio/transcript handling, remote STT endpoint, and voice-driven tier-3 tool execution bypassing HITL
entries.evidence: Named controls on every hop: (a) recognition is the platform speech_to_text plugin (lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/voice_input_service.dart:33-81, 202-208) — no audio buffer or temp file is created by app code and no audio is uploaded to a project-owned STT endpoint; (b) the transcript is not concatenated into a system prompt — it is dispatched as a normal user message (voice_turn_service.dart:192 dispatcher.dispatch(transcript) -> chat_voice_prompt_dispatcher.dart:114 cubit.sendMessage(trimmed)), so it carries no more authority than typed text and is subject to the same tier gate at tool_registry.dart:238-262; (c) the HITL gate is not bypassed by voice: a tier-3 tool pauses the turn and the dispatcher returns VoiceTurnNeedsApprovalFailure (chat_voice_prompt_dispatcher.dart:125-127) without approving anything — approveAction is reachable only from the user's sheet tap (chat_screen.dart:1577-1585, :2010); (d) the turn is single-flight (voice_turn_service.dart:76-79 _active, :94-99 isListening check). Residual, recorded as its own row: the intent-supplied action extra can start such a turn with no tap.

entries.risk_area: Arbitrary action string reaching tool execution / prompt injection through the action channel
entries.evidence: Named control: the payload-to-action handler accepts only the three literals 'voice_input', 'cancel_voice', 'quick_status' after normalisation (lib/presentation/voice/voice_turn_action_listener.dart:162-178, switch on action.toLowerCase().trim()). Any other string, including a tool name or prompt, falls through with no effect — there is no path from this string into ToolRegistry.executeTool. So the action extra cannot name a tool or supply prompt text; it can only start the fixed mic turn or the fixed quick_status prompt. The consequence that DOES survive (an unauthenticated third-party app starting that turn without a tap) is tracked in its own coverage entry, because the control here bounds what the string can say, not who may say it.

entries.surface: Pocket Node, Node/Geofence screens, Gateway screens (pocket_node_screen.dart, geofence_management_screen.dart, gateway_link_cubit.dart, gateway_rpc_cubit.dart)
entries.risk_area: Screen-level surface review for autonomous action, credential display, and unsanitised input
entries.evidence: Review scope: lib/presentation/screen/pocket_node/pocket_node_screen.dart, lib/presentation/screen/node/geofence_management_screen.dart + cubit, lib/presentation/screen/gateway/ (gateway_link_cubit.dart, gateway_rpc_cubit.dart). Findings: (a) pocket_node renders status only — endpoint, connection state, service list — and its diagnostic/ping handlers (pocket_node_screen.dart:397-420) are local UI stubs, with the endpoint taken from the stored active profile (:330-343) rather than from any input; no credential is displayed; (b) geofence entries are persisted through the same encrypted store (secure_storage_service.dart:338-343) and can be created by the tier-1 auto tool register_geofence (tool_registry.dart:968-975), but the only effect of a geofence is a local Action Center item with a display payload (ambient_trigger_service.dart:175-192), which the action-center entry already cleared as non-executing; (c) the gateway RPC cubit is the one surface where remote frames DO reach tool execution — that path is owned and covered by the gateway/tool-registry entries (tier gate at gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:88-104, execution at :143-152) and the read_web_page gate defect is filed under the share-intent entry. No new issue in this slice.
