entries.surface: Remote skill import pipeline: SkillSecurityScanner.scan → SkillImportPreview.canImport → SkillImportService.confirmImport (lib/domain/services/skills/skill_security_scanner.dart:149-190, lib/domain/entities/skills/skill_scan.dart:41-57, lib/domain/entities/skills/skill_import_preview.dart:20-21, lib/domain/services/skills/skill_import_service.dart:59-75)
entries.risk_area: Prompt injection / security-control that does not gate — advisory-only scanner cannot block import of an injection payload
entries.evidence: RESOLVED from needs_follow_up to ruled_out as a vulnerability. Named controls, all user-consent gates verified at file:line: (1) exactly one import entry point — `skills_hub_screen.dart:131` opens `SkillImportDialog`; the user must supply the URL and tap Fetch (`skill_import_dialog.dart:108`), and `registerSkillFromMarkdown`/`registerSkill` (`skills_cubit.dart:113-120`) have NO production caller at all; (2) the preview warns before import — findings rendered as 'Possible injection patterns (advisory): <patternIds>' in amber (`skill_import_dialog.dart:194-195`, :202) with Import as a separate deliberate tap (`:216`); (3) `applyImportPolicy` forces `isEnabled: false` (`skill_security_scanner.dart:189-190`); (4) enabling requires the explicit hub toggle (`skills_hub_screen.dart:313-327` → `setSkillEnabled` `skills_registry_service.dart:249-257`) and the persisted `skill_states` row is written with the already-false value (`:213`), so hydration (`:163-170`) cannot resurrect it; (5) a remote skill cannot register new tools (`DocBuilderSkill.registerTools` is DI-bootstrap-only, `injection.config.dart:391-393`); (6) the skill `tools` list grants nothing new because every tool defaults to enabled (`tool_registry.dart:210`, :222). RESIDUAL HARDENING OBSERVATION (not a finding): the scanner cannot block a payload (`scan()` :149-185 only builds `unknownTools`; `isRejected => hasUnknownTools` at `skill_scan.dart:47`), `isClean` (:50) is therefore true for a skill with critical findings and is currently test-only (no production caller), and `buildSystemPrompt` (`skills_registry_service.dart:362-379`) concatenates skill text into the system prompt with no untrusted-data delimiter. Static-only: no emulator, no Dart toolchain, so nothing was executed.

entries.risk_area: SSRF / redirect-based host escape / oversized-document DoS on skill fetch
entries.evidence: Control: same-host redirect enforcement at skill_remote_loader.dart:80-88 — `resolvedUri.host != currentHost` returns NetworkFailure and the next request is never issued (manual following with `followRedirects: false` at :64, so no post-hoc check is possible to bypass); fail-closed on missing Location (:75-79) and on >3 hops (:71-73). Size cap is enforced twice: declared Content-Length before touching the stream (:95-101) and a running byte count during streaming (:109-120). validateSourceUrl only enforces the transport shape (https + host) but the LAN-hop risk it declines to cover is closed by the same-host policy.

entries.risk_area: Credential redirection to attacker-chosen origin
entries.evidence:
Adversarial re-test of the split-write negative; it holds on every path I could construct — no code path pairs a NEW base URL with a PRE-EXISTING stored key.

(1) Writers of the stored base URL. `SecureStorageService.saveBaseUrl` (lib/data/datasources/local/settings/secure_storage_service.dart:59-61) is the only writer of `llm_base_url` (grep for `llm_base_url`/`keyBaseUrl` across lib/ returns nothing else). It has exactly three callers and each writes the key in the same operation: `saveSettings` (:131-148, key at :140), `setActiveServerProfile` (:281-288, key at :284), and `ServerProfileCubit.addProfile`'s `Future.wait` (server_profile_cubit.dart:140-145). The only other `saveApiKey` caller is `resetToDefaults`' clear (settings_cubit.dart:197). `resetToDefaults` (:189-210) writes `AppConstants.defaultBaseUrl` — a compile-time const `'https://api.openai.com/v1'` (lib/common/constant.dart:5) that no attacker input reaches — and preserving the key there keeps URL+credential matched (the key belongs to that origin); its only production caller is the AppBar reset button (settings_screen.dart:155). `saveServerProfile`/`saveServerProfiles` (secure_storage_service.dart:189-241) touch only the profile list, never `llm_base_url`; `deleteServerProfile` (:244-248) is reached only from `deleteProfile` (server_profile_cubit.dart:282) and re-syncs via `setActiveServerProfile` (:286), i.e. both fields together.

(2) URL vs credential source. Every credential sink takes both from one call site: chat_datasource.dart:38-54 (baseUrl+apiKey params from the same AgentCubit snapshot, agent_cubit.dart:924-929, populated together at :481-492 from a single `getSettings()` read); server_profile_probe_service_impl.dart:23,70 (URL and token typed by the same user in the same form); voice_output_service.dart:227/255 (both from stored settings, with ZERO awaits between :227 and :255 — verified by counting, so no interleaving write can split the pair); gateway_client.dart:175-220 (token is the parameter passed with that URL; chat_screen.dart:1223 passes `payload.gatewayUrl`+`payload.token` from the same payload). No Interceptor, no default `Options`/`BaseOptions` header and no `HttpClient` exists anywhere in lib/ (modules.dart:14-17 sets timeouts only; `Interceptor` has zero hits), so nothing can attach a stored key to a request whose URL came from elsewhere.

(3) `ServerProfile.copyWith` (server_profile.dart:28-49) allows single-field updates, so I read every call site: secure_storage_service.dart:220/230/272/276 pass only `isActive`; server_profile_cubit.dart:318 passes only `lastConnected`; server_profile_cubit.dart:235-240 passes `gatewayUrl` AND `token` together from the same form submit (settings_screen.dart:144-149). No site replaces `gatewayUrl` while retaining a prior `token`.

(4) Non-pairing routes: manual paste is the same `_handleBarcode` path (qr_scanner_screen.dart:250); Add-Profile (add_profile_screen.dart:411-425) creates a new profile with `makeActive:false` (addProfile :139 only syncs when it becomes active, and then writes both from that form); `MainActivity.extractActionFromIntent` (MainActivity.kt:73-85) reads only `extra_flames_action` into a fixed three-value switch (voice_turn_action_listener.dart:162-178); the share path (share_target_cubit.dart, share_target_service.dart) maps payloads to chat prompts only; `GatewayDeviceRpcReceiver.handleRequest` (gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:68-176) only calls `toolRegistry.executeTool`, and no registered tool writes base URL/key.

I could not name any control that fails on these paths because none exists — the control is structural: the two values are always written and read as a matched pair from one payload/source.

entries.risk_area: Plaintext exposure of chat session titles (first 40 chars of user messages) at rest and in backup
entries.evidence: Resolved by another agent's report. The backup half of this candidate is now filed as vuln-0002 ("Sensitive app data included in Android backups because allowBackup is unset"), which explicitly names flames_chat.db and the sessions/title column and traces them into the default backup include set. That was the missing piece here: the plaintext-at-rest observation had no named exposure path, and the backup channel supplies one on every Android device with cloud backup or device transfer enabled. The residual on-device scenario (a rooted device or a forensic image of /data) is not claimed by vuln-0002 and is not separately reported, since it requires host-level access that the app cannot defend against.
entries.recorded_by: Baseline SAST Secrets And Build Hygiene

entries.risk_area: Untrusted-input validation / missing destination allowlist (phishing + credential disclosure to attacker origin)
entries.evidence: Resolved — filed as vuln-0012. Independently re-verified every hop by reading the source: `PairingParser.parse` (lib/domain/tools/pairing/pairing_parser.dart:53-56) is the sole destination control and admits any `http`/`https` authority with no https-only rule, no host allowlist, no same-origin comparison and no `userInfo` rejection (so `https://trusted.example@pair.evil.example` passes and the socket goes to `pair.evil.example`). Both entry points confirmed: qr_scanner_screen.dart:147-168 (camera) and :170-258 → :250 (manual paste) both pop the payload to the caller. Activation confirmed at chat_screen.dart:1206-1224 (`addFromPairingPayload(payload, makeActive: true)` at :1209, then `_mode = ChatMode.gateway` and connect/auth at :1218/:1223) and settings_screen.dart:158-171. Transmission confirmed at gateway_client.dart:211-216 (auth frame sent immediately after the socket opens) via normalizeGatewayUri :141-165 and gateway_socket.dart:71-74 (plain dart:io, no pinning). Downstream authority confirmed: tool manifest at gateway_client.dart:240-249/:299-307, RPC dispatch at gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:148, self-granting Tier-2 checks at file_workspace_service.dart:78 and notification_triage_service.dart:201-212, Tier-1 `clipboard_read` at tool_registry.dart:267,273. Not overclaimed: the user's stored LLM key is NOT exfiltrated (addProfile mints a new id at server_profile_cubit.dart:128 and rewrites base URL + key together at :140-145). Confidence medium — no dynamic validation possible (no emulator/adb, and the x86-64 Dart SDK present cannot run on this host).

entries.surface: Exported MainActivity intent handling + Add-Profile manual entry
entries.risk_area: Alternative config-write path with weaker validation (intent/deep link/manual entry)
entries.evidence: Exported `MainActivity` intent filters (`android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:73-115`) surface only `extra_flames_action` and the quick-tile action; `MainActivity.extractActionFromIntent` (MainActivity.kt:73-85) maps them to fixed strings consumed by `VoiceTurnActionListener._handleAction` (`lib/presentation/voice/voice_turn_action_listener.dart:166-188`, cases `voice_input`/`cancel_voice`/`quick_status`). No intent extra reaches `saveBaseUrl`/`saveApiKey`, and no deep link or `app_links`/`uni_links` handler exists. The Add-Profile screen (`lib/presentation/screen/settings/add_profile_screen.dart:411-421`) only calls `addProfile` with user-typed fields, and the probe service (`server_profile_probe_service_impl.dart:23,70`) uses the same typed URL.

entries.surface: Skill enablement state: applyImportPolicy → persistence → hydrateFromStorage re-enable path (lib/domain/services/skills/skills_registry_service.dart:134-178, :188-217, :249-257; lib/data/datasources/local/skills/skills_local_datasource.dart:150-171)
entries.risk_area: Auto-enable of an imported remote skill (untrusted text entering the system prompt without user opt-in)
entries.evidence: Control: applyImportPolicy at skill_security_scanner.dart:189-190 forces `isEnabled: false, isCommunity: true` on every imported skill, and SkillImportService.confirmImport is the only production caller of registerImportedSkill (skill_import_service.dart:70). Swept the re-enable paths: setSkillEnabled (:249-257) is reachable only from SkillsCubit.toggleSkill, which is wired only to the user-facing toggle in skills_hub_screen.dart:313-327; hydrateFromStorage/_hydrate (:163-170) applies loadSkillStates() from the `skill_states` table, but that table is written by saveSkillState with the already-false value at registerImportedSkill (:213), and saveSkillState is otherwise called only from _persistSkillState under an explicit user toggle (:254). registerSkillFromMarkdown/registerSkill have NO production UI caller (grep: only skills_cubit.dart:113-120 definitions plus tests). So an imported skill cannot become active without a deliberate user tap.

entries.risk_area: Tool-privilege escalation via a remote skill's `tools` list / tier change from skill frontmatter
entries.evidence: Control: a skill's `tools` list is consumed only by syncWithToolRegistry (skills_registry_service.dart:386-405), which calls setToolEnabled(name, true) at :403 for active skills and setToolEnabled(name, false) at :397 only for tools of INACTIVE skills that no active skill claims. Since ToolRegistry.register does `_toolEnabledStates.putIfAbsent(tool.name, () => true)` (tool_registry.dart:210) and isToolEnabled defaults `?? true` (:222), every registered tool starts enabled, so a skill naming an already-registered tool grants nothing the user did not already have. Unknown tool names are the one rejection path (skill_security_scanner.dart:178-184) and no UI exposes a tool-enable toggle (grep for setToolEnabled in lib/presentation/ returns nothing), so a skill cannot override a user's manual disable choice either.

entries.surface: Gateway WebSocket JSON-RPC frame handling (GatewayDeviceRpcReceiver / GatewayRpcCubit)
entries.risk_area: Remote frame re-points stored credential / bypasses tool tier gate
entries.evidence: `GatewayDeviceRpcReceiver.handleRequest` (`lib/domain/services/gateway/gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:68-176`) only calls `toolRegistry.executeTool(request.tool, request.arguments)`, and no registered tool writes endpoint configuration: grepping `saveBaseUrl|saveApiKey|saveSettings|saveServerProfile` across `lib/domain` and `lib/data/datasources/tools` returns no writer (only `voice_output_service.dart`/`overlay_bubble_service.dart` read SecureStorageService). The RPC frame schema carries `tool` + `arguments` only. Tier-3 tools do gate: `gateway_rpc_cubit.dart:149-155` emits `GatewayRpcWaitingApproval` and blocks on a Completer until the user approves or rejects. What the gateway DOES gain is durable device-tool authority (tool manifest sent post-auth, `gateway_client.dart:301-303`), which is part of the pairing finding rather than a separate config-redirection bug.

entries.risk_area: Insufficient user-visible confirmation of new trust destination
entries.evidence: Resolved — carried as a component of vuln-0012 rather than left open. Confirmed there is no pre-connection confirmation of the destination: the only user-visible feedback is a success snackbar echoing the payload-supplied `profileName` (chat_screen.dart:1226-1237, settings_screen.dart:173-180), shown AFTER `addFromPairingPayload` has persisted the profile and after `startWithProfile`/`connect` has opened and authenticated the socket. No preview, no origin display, no confirm/cancel step exists anywhere in the pairing path (searched lib/presentation/screen/pairing/ and lib/presentation/screen/server_profiles/). This is the missing control that makes the attacker-controlled destination non-obvious to the user, and it is the primary recommended remediation in vuln-0012.

entries.risk_area: Continuous/background sensitive-data collection (location, geofence)
entries.evidence: The periodic background task registered by schedulePeriodicCheck does no collection: the Workmanager callback dispatcher is a no-op — `void ambientWorkmanagerCallbackDispatcher() { Workmanager().executeTask((taskName, inputData) async => true); }` (lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/ambient_trigger_service.dart:17-19) returns true without reading location, battery, or health. Geofence checks are pull-only via the agent tool: `checkAll` is called from exactly one non-service site, tool_registry.dart:1051 (the ambient check tool), and `checkGeofence` requires latitude/longitude to be supplied by the caller. `schedulePeriodicCheck` is invoked only from the Pocket Node UI screen (pocket_node_screen.dart:237), not automatically at app start. So there is no unattended continuous location or device-data collection.

entries.surface: External camera (UVC) preview + capture, and camera_take_photo
entries.risk_area: Camera frame upload to an unvalidated/attacker-chosen URL
entries.evidence: Camera frames never touch a network path in the app's own code: external_camera_service.dart contains no http/url/socket/upload references (grep returns nothing) and the plugin is flutter_ffi_uvc ^1.0.0 (pubspec.yaml:41). The preview is a local Flutter texture created and attached in external_camera_preview_cubit.dart:118-162; a still frame is captured and returned as raw base64 JPEG (tool_registry.dart:520-524) which becomes a tool result to the user's own configured LLM. There is no URL for frames at all, so the 'is the frame upload URL validated' question is not applicable. camera_take_photo (built-in) is likewise tier2Permission with only a permission check and no alternate endpoint.

entries.surface: Tier-3 HITL approval modal (action_approval_sheet.dart) + approveAction execution path
entries.risk_area: HITL approval TOCTOU / benign-summary-vs-real-arguments bypass
entries.evidence: lib/presentation/screen/chat/widgets/action_approval_sheet.dart:45 renders `const JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ').convert(request.parameters)` and :68 shows `request.name` — the approval UI displays the ACTUAL arguments. The same map object is passed through unchanged: agent_cubit.dart:754-758 builds ToolCallRequest with `parameters: arguments`, and approveAction (:606-614) executes `pending.parameters` with no mutation between approval and execution. No TOCTOU / summary-vs-executed mismatch on the Tier-3 path.

entries.surface: ReAct tool-result channel: agent_cubit.dart:766-777, :820-825 → ChatMessage.toWireJson (lib/domain/entities/chat/chat_message.dart:116-127) → agent_cubit.dart:906-930
entries.risk_area: Indirect prompt injection — attacker-controlled tool output replayed to the model as an unframed instruction channel
entries.evidence: Resolved by filed reports that cover this channel class from three angles: vuln-0004 (accessibility-tree channel, high/CVSS 8.1), vuln-0010 (notification channel, medium/CVSS 4.2), and vuln-0013 (fetched-web-page channel feeding the same unframed role:'tool' replay, low/CVSS 3.7). The mechanics this entry recorded are confirmed verbatim in those reports: tool results are appended as `ChatMessage(role:'tool', ...)` at agent_cubit.dart:820-825 (auto-execute) and :647-652 (post-approval), re-serialized unchanged by `toWireJson` (chat_message.dart:116-127), and replayed each turn at agent_cubit.dart:906 → :923-930. No delimiter, wrapper or instruction-hierarchy marker exists anywhere in lib/, and there is no base system prompt in the default configuration (agent_cubit.dart:916 calls buildSystemPrompt() with no basePrompt; skills_registry_service.dart:334-335 returns '').
entries.recorded_by: Tool Tier Gate And Prompt Injection

entries.surface: Tier enforcement points: agent_cubit.dart:742-762 (approval gate + dispatch), tool_registry.dart:238-262 (executeTool), gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:89-151, tool_call_text_parser.dart:214-235
entries.risk_area: Tool tier-gate bypass — invoking a Tier-3 tool without HITL, or downgrading a tier from remote input
entries.evidence: Control: the HITL gate is a direct equality test on the tier constant stored at registration — `if (registered.securityTier == SecurityTier.tier3Hitl)` at agent_cubit.dart:753, with `registered` from `_toolRegistry.getTool(toolName)` (:730). securityTier is set literally per RegisteredTool in tool_registry.dart (verified for all 44 registrations by scripted extraction: 24 tier1Auto / 16 tier2Permission / 4 tier3Hitl) and is never read from a gateway frame, skill frontmatter, tool result, or model-supplied parameter. Skill frontmatter `tier` is parsed (skills_registry_service.dart:50) but referenced ONLY in display widgets. The fallback text tool-call parser (tool_call_text_parser.dart:214-235) cannot reach a tool that the model could not already call: it validates against `isKnownTool` and then hands off to the same _processPendingToolCalls gate. Gateway RPC path also gates Tier 3 before executing (gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:89-143) and fails closed when no approval callback is wired (:91-104).

entries.risk_area: Remote skill text entering the system prompt without user opt-in
entries.evidence: Control: buildSystemPrompt is only reachable for skills where `isEnabled == true` — `getActiveSkills()` filters `.where((s) => s.isEnabled)` (skills_registry_service.dart:296-297) and buildSystemPrompt returns `basePrompt ?? ''` when the active list is empty (:333-336). Combined with applyImportPolicy forcing isEnabled=false (:189-190) and the ruled-out re-enable path (entry d1b975), a freshly imported community skill contributes NOTHING to the system prompt until the user explicitly enables it. What remains is the residual fact that enabled-skill text is concatenated verbatim at :362-379 with no delimiter (consumed at agent_cubit.dart:916-921) — recorded as an observation attached to the import-pipeline entry d68232 rather than as a separate finding, since the entry precondition is a deliberate user action.

entries.risk_area: Remote gateway RPC invoking a Tier-3 device tool without HITL approval
entries.evidence: Control: gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:89-104 — when `onApprovalRequired` is null the handler returns an error frame ('requires user approval, but no approval handler was registered') and never reaches executeTool at :148. Wiring at modules.dart does not pass a callback, and GatewayRpcCubit injects one per-call at gateway_rpc_cubit.dart:138, so the remote path cannot invoke a Tier-3 tool headlessly. Recorded separately from the agent-loop gate because it is an independent entry point (the remote server, not the model, chooses the tool name and arguments).

entries.surface: FlamesNotificationListenerService — binder exposure and static state reachability
entries.risk_area: Binder surface / cross-app access to captured notification data
entries.evidence: FlamesNotificationListenerService is exported but gated by android:permission="android.permission.BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE" (AndroidManifest.xml:126), a signature-level system permission, so no third-party app can bind or start it. The class exposes no Binder interface: onBind returns the NotificationListenerService superclass behaviour and there is no additional public binder method. Its companion object state is private: notificationBuffer and instance are both private (FlamesNotificationListenerService.kt:19-20); only getRecentNotifications/clearBuffer/isConnected are public and those are called exclusively from MainActivity's in-process MethodChannel handler (MainActivity.kt:124-135), not over IPC. Cross-app reach would require the app's own UID or the system, so no third-party app can read the notification buffer.

entries.risk_area: Cross-app access to accessibility tree data / exported settings activity
entries.evidence: FlamesAccessibilityService is exported but gated by android:permission="android.permission.BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE" (AndroidManifest.xml:136), a signature-level system permission, so only the system can bind it. The config declares canRetrieveWindowContent="true" (accessibility_service_config.xml:6) with flagRetrieveInteractiveWindows — that is inherent to the feature the user opts into, not an exposure to other apps, because AccessibilityService window content is readable only by the service itself. No android:settingsActivity is declared anywhere in android/ (grep = 0 hits), so there is no exported settings trampoline. Companion state is private: instance is private (FlamesAccessibilityService.kt:22); captureTree/isConnected/isEnabledInSettings are called only from MainActivity's in-process MethodChannel handler (MainActivity.kt:170-190). Another app cannot reach the captured screen tree.

entries.surface: ToolRegistry tier resolution + SecurityTier assignment paths
entries.risk_area: Remote-controlled tier downgrade (gateway frame / skill package / tool result mutating a tool's tier)
entries.evidence: `RegisteredTool.securityTier` is a `final SecurityTier` set only from compile-time constants in tool_registry.dart (e.g. :708, :742, :899) and RegisteredTool's const constructor (:53-60). Verified no remote input can write it: the only SecurityTier assignment outside tool_registry.dart is doc_builder_skill.dart:62 (a local constant). Skill frontmatter `tier` is display-only metadata, not consulted by any gate (grep `securityTier` across lib/domain/services/skills/, lib/data/datasources/skills/, lib/data/datasources/remote/skills/ returns only doc_builder_skill.dart:62). The tier read at agent_cubit.dart:753 comes from `_toolRegistry.getTool(toolName)` (:730) → the local registered constant. So the gate decision itself cannot be downgraded by a gateway frame, skill package, or tool result.

entries.surface: Storage path selection for SQLite (memory, skills, chat) and Hive
entries.risk_area: Secret exposure via world-readable / external storage locations
entries.evidence: No path uses external/public storage: no getExternalStorageDirectory/getDownloadsDirectory/Environment or /sdcard references in lib/ or android/app/src/main/kotlin. All storage roots are app-private — sqflite getDatabasesPath() with a getApplicationDocumentsDirectory() fallback (sqlite_memory_datasource.dart:85-107, local_memory_service.dart:88-107, skills_local_datasource.dart:48-66, chat_local_datasource.dart:64-68) and Hive.initFlutter('flames') under the app documents dir (myapp.dart:47). Credentials only ever pass through flutter_secure_storage.
entries.recorded_by: Secrets At Rest And In Logs

entries.risk_area: Prompt injection / attacker-controlled screen text gaining instruction authority
entries.evidence: Confirmed by source trace: captureTree() collects text/contentDescription of every node of the foreground app (FlamesAccessibilityService.kt:73-86), the serialized tree is returned unframed as the tool result (accessibility_inspector_service.dart data-layer:135-142), and it becomes a role:'tool' message (agent_cubit.dart:820-825). No untrusted-data marker anywhere on the path; the repo's SkillSecurityScanner has exactly one production caller (skill_import_service.dart:44). Amplified by Tier-1 save_memory (tool_registry.dart:899) and memory re-injection as role:'system' (agent_cubit.dart:907-914). Filed as vuln-0004. Not dynamically validated (no device/emulator/model).

entries.risk_area: Sensitive data exposure — password field text captured from other apps
entries.evidence: captureTree() never calls AccessibilityNodeInfo.isPassword(); the identifier appears nowhere in the android/ or lib/ trees (repo-wide search). Whether the platform already redacts password text before an accessibility service sees it is device/OEM dependent and could NOT be verified — no device, no emulator, no adb. The missing client-side control is established; actual secret capture is not. Fix included as a second part of vuln-0004 (skips isPassword nodes and their subtrees); device verification of both the gap and the fix remains open.

entries.risk_area: Sensitive data flow — permission bypass or unexpected remote destination
entries.evidence: Named control: health_service.dart:195-203 re-checks the per-metric permission against grantedPermissions() before every read and returns a failure when absent, independent of the manifest; tool_registry.dart:1704-1705 additionally gates the tool at Tier 2 with checkPermission(). Records are truncated to 200 (health_service.dart:219-220), returned only as a tool result, and reach no endpoint other than the user's configured LLM/gateway — the repo-wide endpoint search found no alternate destination. Health data is never auto-included in prompts; it requires an explicit model tool call.

entries.risk_area: Background sensitive-data collection (accessibility tree or health data)
entries.evidence: Named control: the service performs no data collection. It is a foreground notification/voice-action service only — it never references FlamesAccessibilityService, FlamesHealthConnect or captureTree. Capture is pull-only: captureTree() has exactly one caller (MainActivity.kt:189, the getScreenTree channel handler) reached only from the Dart platform wrapper, and onAccessibilityEvent (FlamesAccessibilityService.kt:120-122) only records lastEventPackage, which is never read anywhere.

entries.surface: external camera + built-in camera frames (external_camera_capture / camera_take_photo)
entries.risk_area: Camera frame upload to an unexpected endpoint
entries.evidence: Traced: frames are encoded to base64 JPEG and returned as the tool result (tool_registry.dart:520-523), with no upload, multipart POST or alternate destination anywhere in the camera path or the cubit (external_camera_preview_cubit.dart captures and holds frames locally only). Both tools are Tier 2 with permission checks (tool_registry.dart:371, 445); external_camera_capture never raises a permission prompt itself. Frames reach only the user's configured chat-completions endpoint, like any other tool result.

entries.surface: Sensitive device data (location, contacts, NFC, health, camera, screen) → hardcoded or config-driven alternate endpoint
entries.risk_area: Data exfiltration to a non-user-configured remote endpoint
entries.evidence: Repo-wide search for http(s):// literals in lib/ returned only: the sherpa-onnx GitHub release URLs for Piper TTS voices (piper_voice.dart:37,48,59 — model downloads, not device data), wa.me deep links (contact_launcher_tools.dart:128-130), the default api.openai.com base URL (constant.dart:5), and UI placeholder text. No device data is sent anywhere except the user's configured LLM/gateway base URL. The sensitive-data tools are tier-gated (get_location/nfc_*/search_contacts Tier 2; open_whatsapp_chat/make_phone_call Tier 3 HITL), which bounds automated misuse.

entries.surface: ToolRegistry.execute closure invocation paths (tool.execute direct calls)
entries.risk_area: Tier gate bypass via a direct tool-execute path
entries.evidence: No bypass: the only call sites of `tool.execute(...)` in lib/ are tool_registry.dart:257 itself (`grep -rn '\.execute(' lib/` returns only sqlite `db.execute` elsewhere). `executeTool` has exactly 3 callers: agent_cubit.dart:611 (approveAction), agent_cubit.dart:766 (ReAct loop), gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:148. All three route through the single Tier-2 gate at :250.

entries.surface: RegisteredTool.securityTier provenance (remote skill package / gateway frame / tool result)
entries.risk_area: Remote tier tampering / tier downgrade by untrusted input
entries.evidence: Tier is not attacker-influenceable: `RegisteredTool(` is constructed only in tool_registry.dart (all const literals) and lib/data/datasources/skills/doc_builder_skill.dart:39. `Skill.tier` frontmatter is never consulted by any gate (skills_registry_service.dart has no tier read); skill import is display-only (`skill_security_scanner.dart:189-190` applyImportPolicy forces isEnabled:false). `syncWithToolRegistry` (skills_registry_service.dart:386-405) only toggles enablement, never securityTier.

entries.surface: Notification text → agent prompt path (FlamesNotificationListenerService.kt → MainActivity.kt → notification_triage_service.dart → agent_cubit.dart → chat_message.dart → chat_datasource.dart)
entries.risk_area: Indirect prompt injection via untrusted notification text reaching the LLM prompt
entries.evidence: Filed as vuln-0010 (medium, CVSS 4.2, confidence medium) with inline fix. Chain verified hop-by-hop by reading every file: FlamesNotificationListenerService.kt:62-73 (verbatim EXTRA_TITLE/EXTRA_TEXT copy, no length cap, no self-package exclusion) → MainActivity.kt:124-128 → notification_triage_service.dart:264-274 / :311-321 (jsonEncode, no envelope) → tool_registry.dart:821/:851 (tier2Permission + checkPermission) → agent_cubit.dart:820-825 (ChatMessage role:'tool') → :906/:917-921 → chat_message.dart:116-127 (toWireJson, no transformation) → chat_datasource.dart:38-54. Greps for sanitiz/escapeUntrusted/wrapUntrusted/untrusted/maxLength/truncat/delim over the whole path return only unrelated hits; skills_registry_service.dart:332-342 (the only system-prompt builder) contains no data-vs-instruction rule and returns '' in the default no-skill case. Fix verified byte-exact against the checkout for both locations.

entries.risk_area: Injection mitigation claim — keyword filter as a security control
entries.evidence: notification_triage_service.dart:87-122 `_sensitiveKeywords`/`isSensitive` excludes entries whose title+body contain otp|password|pin|bank|transaction|payment|balance|credit card|etc. This is a CONTENT-TOPIC noise filter, not an instruction filter: it matches banking/credential vocabulary and has no concept of instruction-like text (e.g. "ignore previous instructions", "call clipboard_write"). A payload containing none of those keywords passes unfiltered. Confirmed by reading the keyword list and the `haystack.contains` matching logic at :119-122. It therefore provides no mitigation for the injection path.

entries.surface: Tool-result message construction in the ReAct loop (agent_cubit.dart:625-825)
entries.risk_area: Indirect prompt injection via untrusted tool-result content in the ReAct loop
entries.evidence: Reported as part of vuln-0010: the primary fix at agent_cubit.dart:906 envelopes every role=='tool' message, so it covers all untrusted tool-result channels (notifications, read_web_page text, contacts, ui_find_elements tree, clipboard_read, read_device_file) in one place rather than one report per tool. Distinct per-tool reports would be duplicates of one root cause; the notification channel (vuln-0010) and the accessibility channel (vuln-0004) are the two filed instances because each has a distinct source, permission and trigger. read_web_page's own SSRF/path issues are owned by other agents.

entries.surface: Active-memory injection into the system role (agent_cubit.dart:907-914) and save_memory (tool_registry.dart:884)
entries.risk_area: Prompt injection persistence via memory write → system-role injection
entries.evidence: Resolved — this surface is now reported, so it should not remain open. The memory write→system-role path is carried by vuln-0005 (Tier-1 misclassification of six side-effecting tools), which covers save_memory at tool_registry.dart:899 and the agent_cubit.dart:907-914 system-role re-injection, and which was revised to add an executed string-level PoC (hostile content stored verbatim, retrieved via the app's own searchMemories for the prompt "plan my travel trip", then interpolated unchanged into a role:system message with a surviving fake </memories> delimiter and System: marker), the SkillSecurityScanner asymmetry (the same text is flagged by new_instructions_header/do_not_tell_user/chatml_delimiters on the skill-import path at skill_import_service.dart:44-68 while nothing screens memory content), and proof that the retrieval precondition is cheap because _sanitizeFtsQuery OR-joins terms and _extractWords retains stopwords. Independent corroboration from agent 489ffbcd, which checked this path separately and found no sanitizer, delimiter wrapper, provenance marker, or untrusted-data framing. See also entries ee6c8e and 4dc650.

entries.risk_area: Tier-2 gate bypass / unvalidated URL launcher reachable from model output
entries.evidence: Shape (b) form (no justifying comment at :1432) BUT neutralised: `contact_launcher_tools.dart:159-163` rejects anything that is not http/https with a non-empty host before `canLaunchUrl`/`launchUrl`, so `intent://`, `market://`, `javascript:`, `file:`, `tel:` are all rejected. No Android runtime permission exists for opening a browser URL, so the absent `checkPermission` skips no permission evaluation. Residual (noted, not claimed): the tool is auto-executable, so model output can pop a browser at an arbitrary https URL with no confirmation — low-severity UI effect, no unauthorized data access.

entries.risk_area: Tier-2 gate bypass / privilege-chaining via system settings launcher
entries.evidence: Shape (b) form (no justifying comment at :1524) BUT neutralised on both sides: Dart allow-list at `intent_launcher_service_impl.dart:223` (`_allowedSettings.contains(normalized)` -> ServerFailure) and Kotlin `when` at `MainActivity.kt:431-446` with `else -> null` -> `result.success(false)`. No Android runtime permission exists for launching a settings page, so the absent `checkPermission` skips no permission evaluation. Residual (assessed, low): the allow-list deliberately INCLUDES `accessibility`, `notification_listener` and `overlay` (`system_settings_allow_list.dart:40-44`, documented as intentional per AGENTS.md §7), and the tool auto-executes, so model/injected text can walk the user to the privilege-granting page with no confirmation — a UI-spoofing/social-engineering primitive, but the user must still perform the toggle, so no unauthorized grant occurs. Mis-tiering (should be Tier 3 HITL) is a distinct root cause, routed to the Tier-1/mis-tiering agent rather than duplicated here.

entries.surface: ai.hermes.flames/.MainActivity ACTION_SEND intent filter (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:78-108) → receive_sharing_intent EXTRA_TEXT → ShareTargetCubit → chat_screen.dart _submitSharedPayloads → _handleSubmitted → AgentCubit.sendMessage
entries.risk_area: Share-intent auto-submit to agent (unverified source of communication channel)
entries.evidence: Reported as vuln-0011 ("Any co-resident app can auto-submit an agent turn through the exported share-target activity, with no user confirmation and an attacker-chosen URL fetch", medium, CVSS 4.0, confidence medium). Full static chain confirmed with no confirmation gate on any hop: AndroidManifest.xml:57-92 (MainActivity exported, no android:permission, ACTION_SEND text/*), :83-108 (image/*, */* and the three SEND_MULTIPLE filters); plugin ReceiveSharingIntentPlugin.kt:120-124 reads EXTRA_TEXT into the JSON `path` field, :186-190 cold start via getInitialMedia, :188 + :205-208 warm start via NewIntentListener with launchMode=singleTop; GeneratedPluginRegistrant.java:129 registration; share_target_service.dart:105-114 maps to SharedPayload; share_target_cubit.dart:26-35 + :42-48; chat_screen.dart:390-397 auto-invokes _submitSharedPayloads with no user action; :531-565 assembles the prompt; :563-564 calls _handleSubmitted; :1501-1505 AgentCubit.sendMessage (direct) / :1522 client.sendChatMessage (gateway). ChatScreen mount confirmed via app_router.dart:28 -> splash_screen.dart:66-108 -> main_navigation_shell.dart:34-42 IndexedStack. Absence of a gate confirmed by repo-wide search: no matches for autoSubmit/autoSend in lib/, none for confirm/consent/showDialog under screen/share, domain/services/share or domain/entities/share, and no share-related key in the settings key list. No caller-identity check anywhere (rg getCallingActivity|getCallingPackage|getCallingUid|checkCallingPermission|getReferrer over android/ and lib/ = 0 hits). Fix shipped inline: chat_screen.dart:563-564 stages the prompt in the composer instead of submitting. Dynamic validation was not possible (no emulator/adb).

entries.surface: Shared-URL auto-fetch: chat_screen.dart:541-542 → UrlReaderService.fetchReadableText (lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/url_reader_service.dart:72-92) → validateUrl (lib/domain/tools/chat/url_reader_service.dart:59-70) → Dio GET with followRedirects:true
entries.risk_area: SSRF / attacker-chosen outbound request from the victim device
entries.evidence: Captured as a secondary aspect of vuln-0011 rather than a standalone finding, and rated honestly as a blind client-side primitive. Confirmed: validateUrl (lib/domain/tools/chat/url_reader_service.dart:59-70) is the only destination control and checks only scheme http/https plus non-empty host — no loopback, RFC1918, link-local or hostname restriction, so 127.0.0.1, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16 and 169.254.169.254 all pass; extractUrl (:10-37) also auto-prefixes bare domains and is applied to arbitrary shared text at chat_screen.dart:537-540; Dio GET uses followRedirects:true (lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/url_reader_service.dart:43-54) with the app-wide singleton (lib/common/injection/modules.dart:13-17, no interceptors); the fetched body is embedded in the prompt via SharedPayload.toPromptWithLinkContext (shared_payload.dart:74-81). Honest limits that keep this below standalone severity: the request originates from the victim's device, not a server; the attacker cannot read the response, so it is blind and not an exfiltration primitive; and the tool-loop consequences depend on model behaviour that was not demonstrated. One unverified reasoning step is recorded in the report's counterevidence: Dart's dart:io HTTP client does not consult Android NetworkSecurityPolicy, so the absent usesCleartextTraffic does not block the http:// case — reasoned from the platform client implementation, not observed. Resolved by filing, so no follow-up remains for this row.

entries.risk_area: Tier-2 gate bypass / unauthorized message composition
entries.evidence: Shape (b) form (silent omission, no justifying comment at :1493) BUT no Android runtime permission exists for composing an email, so the absent `checkPermission` skips no permission evaluation. The sensitive act (sending) is not performed by the app: `intent_launcher_service_impl.dart:190-205` only builds a `mailto:` URI and calls `launchUrl`; the message is a prefill the user must explicitly send from their mail client. Residual (noted, low): the tool auto-executes, so model/injected text can prefill an outbound email (to/subject/body) with no confirmation — a phishing/social-engineering affordance, not an unauthorized send.

entries.risk_area: Tier-2 gate bypass / unauthorized NFC tag read
entries.evidence: Shape (b) form (silent omission, no justifying comment at :1568) BUT there is no runtime permission to evaluate: `android.permission.NFC` is an install-time (normal) permission — Android never shows a runtime dialog for it — and the app declares no runtime NFC permission path. The real gate is physical presence: `nfc_service.dart:260-265` `readCardUid` calls `_platform.scan(...)` and `DefaultNfcPlatformWrapper.runWithCard/scan` (nfc_service.dart:70-80) start an `NfcManager` foreground dispatch session with a 20s timeout that only completes when the user physically taps a tag into the field. A headless invocation cannot read a card without the user presenting one, and the tool's `execute` closure additionally checks `isAvailable()`/`isEnabled()` before scanning. Absent `checkPermission` therefore skips nothing.

entries.risk_area: Tier-2 gate bypass / unauthorized NFC e-money balance read
entries.evidence: Same as `nfc_read_tag`: no runtime permission exists for NFC (install-time normal permission, no dialog), and `nfc_service.dart:280-291` `readEmoneyBalance` goes through `_platform.runWithCard` which requires a live foreground NFC session completed by the user physically tapping a card. The `execute` closure checks `isAvailable()`/`isEnabled()` first. Absent `checkPermission` skips no permission evaluation; the physical tap is the effective gate.

entries.surface: registerNotificationTools — send_local_notification vs schedule_reminder tier split (lib/domain/tools/chat/tool_registry.dart:689-756)
entries.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization / inconsistent tier assignment across tools sharing one service
entries.evidence: Contrast verified: send_local_notification (:692) is tier1Auto at :708 while schedule_reminder (:721) is tier3Hitl at :742; both are registered inside registerNotificationTools(NotificationServiceBase service) declared at :689 against the same service object. domain/tools/chat/notification_service.dart:8-9 and :11/:17 document the split explicitly ('sendLocalNotification: Tier 1 (auto-approve)' / 'scheduleReminder: Tier 3 (HITL required)'); data/datasources/tools/chat/notification_service.dart:74-95 sendLocalNotification calls _plugin.show(...) immediately with model-controlled title/body while :97+ scheduleReminder calls _plugin.zonedSchedule(...). Sending immediately is at least as direct as scheduling for later, so the split is inconsistent under either reading of Tier 1. This inconsistency is the proof that the misclassification is a defect, and it is captured in vuln-0005.

entries.surface: Six tier1Auto tools with device-state side effects (tool_registry.dart:291, :708, :899, :930, :968, :1213)
entries.risk_area: Security-tier misclassification enabling ungated device side effects (clipboard write, notification send, memory write/delete, geofence, background service)
entries.evidence: Verified each of the six tools carries `securityTier: SecurityTier.tier1Auto` with 8-space indentation at the exact lines cited in vuln-0005, and confirmed by per-block grep (line ranges 279-300, 692-716, 884-901, 921-933, 953-982, 1168-1345) that NONE declares a checkPermission callback. Consequence documented in the report: because tool_registry.dart:250-251 is `requiresPermission(tier) && tool.checkPermission != null`, assigning any of these to Tier 2 would be a silent no-op, which is why the fix uses tier3Hitl. The tier value is a local const at registration and no remote input (gateway frame, skill package, tool result, model parameter) can alter it — consistent with entries 4fa5bc/429507/21df47.

entries.surface: Memory vault persistence path: save_memory/delete_memory → local_memory_service.dart → sqlite_memory_datasource.dart (flames_memory.db)
entries.risk_area: Ungated persistent state write and ungated destruction of user data
entries.evidence: Write: save_memory (tool_registry.dart:884/:899 tier1Auto) → local_memory_service.dart:498 saveMemoryFormattedJson → saveMemory → sqlite_memory_datasource.dart:190 db.insert('memories', ...) into the on-disk DB `flames_memory.db` (:16), so content survives app restart. Delete: delete_memory (tool_registry.dart:921/:930 tier1Auto) → local_memory_service.dart:570 deleteMemoryFormattedJson → sqlite_memory_datasource.dart:343 deleteMemory / :357 deleteMemoryByKey, both issuing db.delete('memories', ...) with no confirmation anywhere on the path. SQL parameterisation itself is sound (where: 'id = ?' / 'key = ?' with whereArgs), so injection is not the issue here — the issue is that both operations are ungated, which is captured as the persistence/destruction impact in vuln-0005. SQLi on this datasource was separately ruled out (entries 769a99/987c37).

entries.risk_area: Broken function-level authorization via remote gateway RPC tool invocation
entries.evidence: Second ungated caller: gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:89 tests only `SecurityPolicy.requiresHitl(tool.securityTier)`, then calls `toolRegistry.executeTool` at :148. A remote gateway frame naming a Tier-1 tool therefore reaches executeTool with no HITL and no permission evaluation — same gap as the local ReAct path, different entry point. This is a distinct ingress for the same root cause (reported in vuln-0005), not a separate defect. Note: the nullable approval callback (:90-104) fails closed for Tier 3 when unwired, so only the Tier-1 gap applies here.

entries.surface: Tool enablement defaults + bundled skill tool lists (skills_registry_service.dart)
entries.risk_area: Reachability / default-enabled tool exposure
entries.evidence: Tools are enabled without user action: `ToolRegistry.register` sets `_toolEnabledStates.putIfAbsent(tool.name, () => true)` (tool_registry.dart:210) and `isToolEnabled` defaults true (:222). Bundled skills ship enabled (`Skill.isEnabled` defaults true, skill.dart:29) and `syncWithToolRegistry` (:386-405) enables every tool named by an active skill — it only ever DISABLES tools named by inactive skills (:393-400), so it cannot remove an already-enabled tool. `device_memory` (skills_registry_service.dart:644-664) names save_memory/delete_memory; clipboard_write is named at :416/:433/:450/:467; send_local_notification at :568. So the affected tools are live in the default configuration, which removes a "requires opt-in" caveat.

entries.risk_area: Tier-2 gate bypass / covert camera capture without permission
entries.evidence: Shape (b) form (silent omission, no justifying comment at :371) BUT the OS gate covers it: `camera_vision_service.dart:73-79` calls `image_picker` `pickImage(source: ImageSource.camera)`, which launches the system camera Activity as a foreground UI the user must operate, and because the app declares `android.permission.CAMERA` (AndroidManifest.xml:14) Android enforces that permission for the capture intent. A denial surfaces as `PermissionFailure` at `camera_vision_service.dart:100-107` (PlatformException permission mapping). The contrast tool's checker is check-only anyway (`external_camera_service.dart:265-267` -> `Permission.camera.status`, no request), so the omitted pre-check changes only the error message, not the authority. `retrieveLostData()` (:50-68) re-surfaces an image the user already captured in a prior session, not a new covert capture.

entries.risk_area: Sensitive-data control bypass / second-factor disclosure to remote LLM
entries.evidence: Confirmed and filed as vuln-0008. Root cause: extractLatestOtp (notification_triage_service.dart:277-310) calls _loadEntries directly at :284 and never consults isSensitive, so the OTP/banking/password exclusion applied by the sibling getRecentNotifications at :249-252 is bypassed; the live code is returned in OtpExtractionResult (:290-297, toJson 'otp' at lib/domain/tools/chat/notification_triage_service.dart:79-89). Registered Tier-2 auto-execute at tool_registry.dart:871, so no per-use confirmation (agent_cubit.dart:759-766 pauses only for tier3Hitl). Result transmitted off-device on two sinks: local ReAct loop to the configured LLM API (agent_cubit.dart:820-825, :906, :923-930) and gateway RPC to the remote Hermes server (gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:166-171). Privacy intent evidenced by the test named 'filters out sensitive entries for privacy' (notification_triage_service_test.dart:375). Fix filed inline: tool_registry.dart:871 tier2Permission -> tier3Hitl, which closes all three executeTool call sites. Static-only: no device/emulator, so extraction and transmission were not executed (confidence medium).

entries.surface: Residual Tier-1 side-effecting tools: speak_text, open_map_navigation, list_device_files
entries.risk_area: Tier-1 misclassification (residual instances not included in the filed fix set)
entries.evidence: Three further Tier-1 tools have side effects but were deliberately excluded from the fix set in vuln-0005 as lower-impact: `speak_text` (tool_registry.dart:1119, tier :1138) speaks arbitrary model text aloud; `open_map_navigation` (:1442, tier :1462) launches an external app via a geo intent; `list_device_files` (:793, tier :809) performs ungated recursive directory enumeration (its file-read aspect is owned by another agent). Same root cause as the reported defect but not remediated by the six tier changes; flagged for follow-up rather than silently dropped.

entries.surface: AgentCubit._pendingToolCall approval slot (agent_cubit.dart:64, :752-762, :602-614) with unguarded second-turn entry points (share intent, NFC)
entries.risk_area: HITL approval-gate integrity across concurrent turns (shared pending-approval slot overwrite -> approving one tool may execute another)
entries.evidence: Distinct from the already-recorded single-turn check (entry c8730f, which asked whether the sheet's displayed arguments match the executed ones — they do, same map object). This row is the CROSS-TURN case: approval is bound to the shared mutable slot `_pendingToolCall` (agent_cubit.dart:64) rather than to the request the user is looking at. `_processPendingToolCalls` assigns the slot then emits `WaitingApproval` (:759-761); `approveAction` re-reads the slot (:606-614) and never compares it with `state.request`. A second turn can start while a tier-3 approval is pending because `sendMessage` has no busy/awaiting-approval guard (:502-536, it only bumps `_runGeneration`), and two unguarded entry points reach it — the exported share intent (chat_screen.dart:386-398 -> :531-565 -> :1494+) and the NFC trigger (agent_cubit.dart:561-580). If that second turn also pauses on a tier-3 tool, the slot is overwritten with a different request while the older sheet is still mounted (the listener pushes a new modal at chat_screen.dart:1572-1585 and never dismisses the previous one; the sheet is isDismissible:false / enableDrag:false with PopScope canPop:false at action_approval_sheet.dart:29-48). A tap landing in the window between the overwrite emit and the new sheet being pushed would execute the request that was never displayed. I could NOT name a control that closes this: the `if (state is! WaitingApproval) return;` guard at :603 only covers the case where the state has already left WaitingApproval (e.g. after `stop()`, which nulls the slot at :844 and emits AgentIdle at :846), and it does not detect that the slot was replaced by a different request while the state stayed WaitingApproval. I also could not confirm it — it needs a real device to observe the emit-to-push frame window and to make the model emit a second tier-3 call, and no emulator/adb exists in this environment. Recorded as open rather than ruled out.

entries.risk_area: NFC tag triggering an autonomous agent prompt from attacker-supplied content
entries.evidence: Named control: an NFC tap dispatches a prompt ONLY when the tag UID already has a binding the user created in Settings. `scanNfcAndDispatchPrompt` (lib/presentation/screen/chat/cubit/agent_cubit.dart:561-580) returns false before `sendMessage` unless `NfcPromptResolver.resolve(uid)` finds a binding (:576-577), and the resolver matches the card UID exactly after trim/lowercase against bindings read from the encrypted store (lib/domain/services/tools/nfc_prompt_resolver.dart:10-18; secure_storage_service.dart:321-331). The bindings themselves are written only from the Settings UI confirmation flow (settings_cubit.dart:340-346, settings_screen.dart:1144). So an attacker-controlled NFC tag cannot supply or select a prompt; it can only trigger a prompt the device owner already bound to that exact card, which is the feature working as intended. The dispatch also goes through the normal `sendMessage` path and therefore remains subject to the tier gate (this is the same path as the open approval-slot row above, which is recorded separately).

entries.surface: chat_datasource.dart + server_profile_probe_service_impl.dart redirect handling (followRedirects default true)
entries.risk_area: Credential forwarded to a cross-origin redirect target (Authorization header handling on redirect)
entries.evidence: RESOLVED — ruled out for the redirect vector specifically. dart:io's `_HttpClient.shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect` (sdk/lib/_http/http_impl.dart, applied in `_openUrlFromRequest`) strips `authorization`, `cookie`, `proxy-authorization` and the other sensitive headers unless the redirect target is same-origin (scheme AND host AND port equal). dio's default `followRedirects: true` therefore does not forward the bearer credential to a cross-origin redirect target on either the chat path (chat_datasource.dart:38-52) or the probe path. This is a named control, not an absence of evidence. Separately, the cleartext-exposure half of these same clients (a non-TLS origin, not a redirect) is real and is filed as vuln-0009.

entries.risk_area: Tar-slip / path traversal / symlink escape on archive extraction
entries.evidence:
INDEPENDENTLY RE-CONFIRMED after adversarial retry (was ruled_out; outcome unchanged, evidence strengthened). Built a second harness reproducing the loop verbatim and executed 39 + 30 hand-crafted byte-level tar vectors through the real `archive` 4.0.9 (`BZip2Decoder`→`TarDecoder`→loop). Every vector CONTAINED (0 escapes, canary files checked outside the destination):

PAX `path=` rewriting (tar_decoder.dart:56-86 `nextName`): `../../`, absolute, nested `sub/../../../`, `./..`, backslash, `//tmp/`, prefix-only, trailing space, NUL-embedded, chained PAX headers, newline-in-value splitting, malformed-first-record, `./` component — all either rejected at :242 (`startsWith(prefix)`) or at :244 (`relative.contains('..')`). Only benign in-prefix paths landed (verified control: `PAX path=vits-piper-v/PWN_pax_legit` → written).

GNU long-name (tar_decoder.dart:43-46): `../../`, absolute, traversal+NUL tail, 300-char nested, no-following-entry, and state-leak sequences (LongLink→directory, LongLink→PAX-override) — all rejected by the same two guards.

UStar `filenamePrefix` (tar_file.dart:98-101 `'$filenamePrefix/$filename'`): prefix=`vits-piper-v` + name=`../…`, prefix=`vits-piper-v/..`, prefix=`vits-piper-v/../..`, name=`/tmp/…` — the concatenated name is always caught by the `..` check or confined by `_joinPath` to `<dest>/tmp/…`.

Entry types passing `isFile` (`typeFlag != '5'`): '3' char, '4' block, '6' fifo, '7' contFile, NUL, 'A', 'L', 'x' — content IS yielded (`entry.content` non-null) and IS written, but always under `destDir`; traversal-named variants of '3'/'6'/'7' rejected at :244.

Symlink/hardlink: typeflag '2' with linkname `/etc` → skipped at :240; typeflag '1' hardlink → decoder sets `symbolicLink` from `nameOfLinkedFile` (tar_decoder.dart:100-102) so also skipped; the EMPTY-linkname asymmetry (`isSymbolicLink` is `symbolicLink?.isNotEmpty` — empty linkname ⇒ `false`) was exercised for both '1' and '2': the entry is then treated as a regular file and its bytes are written INSIDE dest — a benign content-write, not a link creation. Confirmed no `Link(` call exists anywhere in `lib/`, so the app never materialises a symlink; write-through-symlink (F1) is therefore unreachable.

Malformed UTF-8: overlong `C0 AE`, overlong NUL `C0 80`, raw `0xFF`, U+FF0E, U+2024 — all decoded as literal non-`.` characters (never normalised to `..` or `/`) and confined.

`voice.id` provenance: hard allowlist. `downloadVoice` takes a `PiperVoiceDescriptor`; the only production caller resolves it via `piperVoiceById(voiceId)` (settings_cubit.dart:475) which returns null for anything outside the const `kPiperVoiceCatalog` (piper_voice.dart:27-61), and the UI passes `id` from that same catalog (settings_screen.dart:765-846). `savePiperVoiceId` has exactly one writer chain (settings_screen → settings_cubit.dart:438 → secure_storage_service.dart:92); no QR, gateway-RPC, skill, or model-output path writes `piper_voice_id` (grepped the full tree). So a separator/`..` cannot reach `voice.id`, `prefix`, or `destDir`.

Destination is app-private: `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` (piper_tts_engine.dart:118) → `/data/user/0/ai.hermes.flames/app_flutter/tts_models/`; no external-storage permission in the manifest.

Post-write steps do not matter: the `isVoiceReady` check (:256-264) and sidecar delete (:265-271) run AFTER the loop but only delete/extend within `<modelsRoot>/<id>`; a mid-loop throw (exercised) leaves a partial dir inside the app-private root, not outside it.

Also executed the FULL `downloadVoice()` end-to-end (MD5 gate + extraction + isVoiceReady + sidecar) against an archive combining PAX + LongLink + UStar traversal entries: completed, all canaries absent, only intended files under `<root>/tts_models/v/`. Note the MD5 gate (piper_tts_engine.dart:221-228) is a fixed compile-time constant digest over a hardcoded GitHub HTTPS URL, so an attacker cannot substitute a malicious tarball without an MD5 second-preimage (infeasible) — the loop only ever sees bytes matching the pinned digest.

Residual (not a finding): a tar entry declaring a larger `fileSize` than the data actually present causes the decoder to read across subsequent headers, so the written file can contain neighbouring header bytes — still confined to dest.

entries.surface: lib/domain/entities/chat/piper_voice.dart:27-61 + piper_tts_engine.dart:198-229 (Piper voice descriptor: digest provenance and download URL)
entries.risk_area: Attacker-controlled artifact or digest / integrity-check bypass
entries.evidence: Both the expected MD5 and the download URL are compile-time `const` catalog entries, not a remote manifest: `tarballMd5`/`downloadUrl` at piper_voice.dart:34-37, 45-48, 56-59. `downloadVoice` receives a `PiperVoiceDescriptor`; the only callers pass `piperVoiceById(voiceId)` (settings_cubit.dart:475-480, :519) or catalog entries, and `downloadPiperVoice` rejects unknown ids with 'Unknown voice'. Verified the hardcoded digests against the real upstream artifacts: en_US-lessac-medium = e7e26d0730b3cb9b451efb3f7f700daf (downloaded 67230653 bytes) and id_ID-news_tts-medium = c91a63c2fa185b6f54609019e19232ef (downloaded 67243848 bytes) — both match. No QR/profile/skill/gateway path writes the descriptor. MD5 is therefore a hardening note only (no collision-resistant primitive), not exploitable: an attacker controls neither the artifact nor the digest.

entries.risk_area: Unbounded download / resource exhaustion; recursive-delete via attacker-influenced voiceId
entries.evidence: No realistic attacker control on either path. The fetch URL is the hardcoded k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx GitHub HTTPS release (piper_voice.dart:36-37) and `tarballSizeBytes` is declared but never enforced anywhere (grep: only the const definitions) — an unbounded-download/DoS concern only against a compromised GitHub origin, outside the threat model, so recorded as robustness, not a finding. `deleteVoice` does `Directory(_joinPath(modelsRoot, voiceId)).delete(recursive: true)` (:277-280) with no `..`/separator check on `voiceId`, but every caller supplies a catalog id from `kPiperVoiceCatalog` (settings_screen.dart:832, :846 via settings_cubit.dart:472-480, :612-623) and `piper_voice_id` in secure storage has no remote writer (only settings_screen.dart:730 → settings_cubit.dart:438). Not attacker-reachable; latent robustness gap only.

entries.risk_area: Tier-2 gate bypass / unauthorized accessibility screen-tree read
entries.evidence: Shape (a) documented intentional omission: `tool_registry.dart:1761-1763` carries the comment "No checkPermission: the registry gate would return a generic PermissionFailure, while the service returns the actionable [accessibility_not_enabled] message the model needs." The service independently enforces status before reading: `accessibility_inspector_service.dart:109-112` returns a Left failure unless `checkStatus() == AccessibilityStatus.active`, and `checkStatus()` (:72-86) reads the platform service-connected/granted state. A non-enabled accessibility service therefore cannot be read.

entries.risk_area: Insecure deserialization / object injection from attacker-controlled skill package
entries.evidence:
INDEPENDENTLY RE-CONFIRMED (ruled_out unchanged; evidence materially extended). Re-ran the parse path against the real pinned `yaml` 3.1.4 with 20 adversarial frontmatter documents, executing `parseSkillFromMarkdown` (skills_registry_service.dart:36-115) verbatim.

Key precision the original entry lacked: the parser does NOT sanitise — it ACCEPTS hostile identifiers and passes them through. Confirmed accepted values: `id: ../../evil` → `Skill.id == "../../evil"`; `id: /etc/passwd` → `Skill.id == "/etc/passwd"`; `id: sub/dir/skill`; the no-frontmatter heading fallback at :99-114 yields `# ../../evil` → `id == "../../evil"` and `# a/b/c` → `id == "a/b/c"`. So the negative is "hostile value accepted but no sink", NOT "hostile value rejected".

YAML-specific vectors executed, all benign: anchor/alias reuse (S5) and a 9-level nested alias fan-out (S6) expand to a bounded scalar/string form and cannot execute or allocate unboundedly — the values only ever reach `.toString()` at :45-56. Duplicate mapping keys throw `Error on line 2, column 1: Duplicate mapping key` and are caught by the `catch (_)` at :79, falling back to the heading parser — no crash, no partial-object state. Non-scalar `id` (a map) stringifies to `"{nested: value}"`; numeric `12345`/boolean `true` coerce via `.toString()`. `tools: clipboard_read` (scalar, not list) is ignored because of the `is YamlList` guard at :59, so a scalar cannot become a tool entry; a nested list `[[clipboard_read]]` becomes the literal string `"[clipboard_read]"`, which cannot match any registered tool name and is therefore rejected by the unknown-tools gate (`SkillScanResult.hasUnknownTools`, skill_scan.dart:41-45). A 5000-element `tools` list parses without error. A NUL in a quoted scalar survives as a literal character; no truncation-based bypass.

Sink re-verification (the reason this stays ruled_out): a full-tree search of the skills pipeline — `lib/data/datasources/local/skills/`, `lib/domain/services/skills/`, `lib/data/datasources/remote/skills/`, `lib/data/datasources/skills/`, `lib/presentation/screen/skills/`, `lib/domain/entities/skills/` — for `File(`/`Directory(`/`writeAs`/`openWrite`/`createSync`/`.join(`/`$dir` returns exactly ONE hit: `File(path).parent.create(recursive: true)` at skills_local_datasource.dart:63, where `path` comes from `sqflite`'s `getDatabasesPath()`/`_databasePath` (the app-private database dir, :52-57) and is never derived from skill data. `skill.id`/`skill.name` are used only as a `Map<String, Skill>` key (skills_registry_service.dart:120-122, :201-213) and as a bound SQLite primary key (`where: 'id = ?'` / `whereArgs`, skills_local_datasource.dart:144-148, :165-170). The skill loader also has no import of or reference to `PiperVoiceStore`/`downloadVoice`, so it cannot reach the tarball extraction path either.

entries.surface: Skill package id/name → filesystem path (skills_registry_service.dart:188-217, doc_builder_skill.dart:91-99)
entries.risk_area: Path traversal / arbitrary file write from package-supplied identifiers
entries.evidence: No path is constructed from package-supplied strings. `skill.id`/`skill.name` are used only as a `Map<String, Skill>` key and SQLite primary key (skills_registry_service.dart:120-122, :201-213; local datasource insert at :132-141 uses bound `where: 'id = ?'`/column values, never interpolation). Grep for `File(`/`Directory(` across lib/domain/services/skills/, lib/data/datasources/local/skills/, lib/data/datasources/remote/skills/ and lib/presentation/screen/skills/ returns no file-write sites. The one adjacent write is doc_builder_skill.dart:91-99, whose `outputFileName`/title is passed through `_slugify` (:125-132) that replaces every char outside [a-z0-9] with '_' and caps at 60 chars, so traversal cannot survive into `<documents>/documents/doc_<slug>_<stamp>.pdf`. A skill package also cannot name a URL: `sourceUrl` comes from the user-typed field (skill_import_dialog.dart:108-110), not from package content.

entries.surface: Skill import enablement and gating (skill_import_service.dart:59-75, skill_security_scanner.dart:187-190)
entries.risk_area: Imported skill enabled by default / missing signature gate
entries.evidence: Every import passes `SkillSecurityScanner.applyImportPolicy` which forces `isEnabled: false, isCommunity: true` (skill_security_scanner.dart:189-190), applied in `SkillImportService.confirmImport` before `registerImportedSkill` (skill_import_service.dart:69-73). Frontmatter `is_enabled: true` is parsed at skills_registry_service.dart:70-71 but is overridden on the import path. The only paths that skip the policy — `SkillsCubit.registerSkillFromMarkdown` (skills_cubit.dart:113) and `SkillsCubit.registerSkill` (:119) — have NO production caller (grep shows only tests), so the shipped ingest path is exclusively importSkillFromUrl → buildPreview → confirmSkillImport. No signature/allowlist exists; the only hard gate is `unknownTools` (skill_scan.dart:82), scanner findings being advisory. Signature absence is a design characteristic, not an exploitable defect on its own.

entries.surface: Whole-app sweep for archive-extraction and download-to-disk pipelines (lib/ + android/)
entries.risk_area: Archive extraction / Zip-Slip in any other pipeline (family sweep)
entries.evidence: Swept lib/ and android/ for every archive/compression/decompression API (`TarDecoder|ZipDecoder|BZip2Decoder|GZipCodec|ExtractFileToDisk|extractArchiveToDisk|ZipInputStream|GZIPInputStream|TarInputStream`): the ONLY extraction pipeline in the entire app is piper_tts_engine.dart:234-235. No other download-and-extract, unzip, or restore path exists, so no sibling instance of this bug class was missed. Other file writers are file_workspace_service.dart:74 (bytes supplied in-process), local_memory_service.dart / sqlite_memory_datasource.dart (SQLite DB creation under app documents), and doc_builder_skill.dart:99 (slugified PDF name).

entries.surface: Extracted Piper model directory (sherpa_onnx consumption path, piper_tts_engine.dart:56-88, 336-357)
entries.risk_area: Code execution / native-library loading from extracted archive content
entries.evidence: No code-execution primitive exists on the extracted content: grep across lib/ for `Process.run|Process.start|chmod|DynamicLibrary|dlopen|loadLibrary|open(` returns nothing, and no Kotlin code handles archives. The extracted `.onnx`/`tokens.txt`/`espeak-ng-data` are consumed only as data-file paths by `sherpa_onnx.OfflineTtsVitsModelConfig` (piper_tts_engine.dart:66-74); the native library itself ships with the app, is not loaded from the extraction directory, and the model files are parsed as data, not executed. So even a hypothetical arbitrary write into that directory would not be an RCE path on its own.

entries.risk_area: Path traversal via model-controlled output filename in the PDF export tool
entries.evidence: `export_document_pdf` is Tier 1 auto (doc_builder_skill.dart:62) and takes `outputFileName`/`title` from model output, so the write path is reachable without HITL — but traversal cannot survive `_slugify` (:125-132): every character outside [a-z0-9] (including '/', '\\', '.') is replaced with '_', leading/trailing '_' stripped, length capped at 60, and empty results become 'document'. The resulting name is joined into `<documents>/documents/doc_<slug>_<timestamp>.pdf` (:97). No `..` sequence can be produced by the transform, so the write is contained to the app documents dir.

entries.surface: Dio configuration (lib/common/injection/modules.dart:13-17) and all credential-bearing HTTPS clients
entries.risk_area: TLS certificate validation bypass / missing pinning for credential-bearing requests
entries.evidence: Client-side TLS verification is left at the platform default: no Dio HttpClientAdapter, no badCertificateCallback, no SecurityContext or certificate-pinning configuration exists anywhere in lib/ (grep for HttpClientAdapter|badCertificateCallback|SecurityContext returns nothing; NetworkModule.provideDio at lib/common/injection/modules.dart:13-17 sets only timeouts). Credentials therefore ride on the same OS-validated TLS as every other request, and a MITM would need a user-installed CA; that is the platform baseline rather than an application defect.

entries.risk_area: Arbitrary file read / unbounded filesystem enumeration (missing path containment + no-op permission gate)
entries.evidence: CONSOLIDATED into entry 85e0c1 (the parent's original row for this same surface), which now carries the full resolution. Reported as vuln-0007. Kept for history: no containment control on either tool path; read_device_file's Tier-2 gate is inert (checkPermission hardcoded `async => true`, file_workspace_service.dart:78); list_device_files is tier1Auto with no gate; path arrives from model output via unvalidated jsonDecode (agent_cubit.dart:723) and auto-executes (only tier3Hitl pauses). Correction applied after self-check: the SQLite databases are NOT readable (blocked by the `db`/`sqlite` denylist and by the SQLite header NUL byte). See 85e0c1 for the authoritative record.

entries.surface: Tier resolution for read_device_file and list_device_files (tool_registry.dart registration + agent_cubit.dart gate)
entries.risk_area: Tier-gate bypass / tier downgrade by remote input
entries.evidence: The tier is read from the local `securityTier` constant on the RegisteredTool at registration (tool_registry.dart:782 and :809) and consumed by the HITL gate at agent_cubit.dart:760-765 and the permission gate at tool_registry.dart:250-255. No remote input (gateway frame, skill package, tool result, model argument) writes to RegisteredTool.securityTier — no such setter exists. So the tier itself cannot be downgraded. The real defect is not a downgrade but that list_device_files is *declared* tier1Auto in the source, and read_device_file's tier2 gate is a no-op; both are covered by the file-read finding.

entries.risk_area: Broad external-storage read (claimed /sdcard access)
entries.evidence: Confirmed no READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE / MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE / WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE anywhere in android/ (grep across the whole android tree returns nothing; AndroidManifest.xml:3-36 lists only INTERNET, calendar, location, camera, contacts, NFC, Health Connect, audio, notifications). Consequence: on modern Android the model cannot read /sdcard — scoped storage + absence of the permission makes those reads fail with EACCES. This genuinely limits the finding's blast radius and is recorded as counterevidence; it does NOT remove the finding, because the app's own private storage (databases/, app_flutter/, shared_prefs/, files/) is fully readable by the same UID with no permission required, and that is where the plaintext SQLite databases live.

entries.surface: Chat history at rest (flames_chat.db) readability by read_device_file
entries.risk_area: Full plaintext chat-transcript disclosure
entries.evidence: Superseded by a stronger conclusion from a later self-check. The plaintext SQLite databases are NOT readable via read_device_file at all, blocked twice over: (1) `db` and `sqlite` are both present in `_binaryExtensions` (file_workspace_service.dart:98-124); (2) a real SQLite file has a NUL byte at offset 15 of its header (`SQLite format 3\x00`), and `_containsNullByte` (:133-140) scans the first 8000 bytes and rejects it independently of the filename. I also confirmed chat message bodies are not in the DB (they are in FlutterSecureStorage, chat_local_datasource.dart:113-125) and that memory-vault content is already model-accessible via the Tier-1 list_memories/search_memories tools (tool_registry.dart:905-945), so file-level access to those DBs would add nothing. My earlier claim that the denylist "does not protect the plaintext databases" was an overclaim; corrected in report vuln-0007.

entries.risk_area: Path traversal / arbitrary file read (CWE-22) via agent tool argument
entries.evidence: Confirmed NO containment control on either tool path: readFile (file_workspace_service.dart:149-175) and listFiles (:224-281) contain no startsWith/resolveSymbolicLinks/canonicalise/base-directory join (verified by targeted harness, exit 0). getDocumentsDirectory() is used only for PDF writes (doc_builder_skill.dart:86). The read_device_file Tier-2 gate is inert because checkPermission is hardcoded true (file_workspace_service.dart:78), and list_device_files is tier1Auto with no gate. Path arrives from model output via unvalidated jsonDecode (agent_cubit.dart:723) and auto-executes (only tier3Hitl pauses, :760-765). Reported as vuln-0007 with an inline, executed-verified fix.

entries.surface: Dynamic validation of read_device_file against app-private storage (databases/flames_memory.db, flames_skills.db)
entries.risk_area: Runtime confirmation of the readable path set (same-UID access to app-private databases)
entries.evidence: No Android build was possible (no emulator, no adb, no running app, no resolved Dart dependencies), so I could not confirm by execution which absolute paths the app process can actually open at runtime, nor observe a real model-emitted tool call reaching the sink. Android semantics make same-UID reads of the app's own private storage the expected behaviour, but that was not observed. The report (vuln-0007) is filed at confidence=medium with this gap named in confidence_rationale, and it is carried as an open item.

entries.risk_area: Plaintext secrets at rest (OTP persisted in chat history)
entries.evidence: Ruled out as a separate plaintext-at-rest finding: agent_cubit.dart:826 -> chat_local_datasource.dart:113-121 _storage.write(...) where _storage is FlutterSecureStorage 9.2.4 (pubspec.lock:544-551; lib/common/injection/modules.dart:23), i.e. EncryptedSharedPreferences. The chat-history copy of the OTP is therefore encrypted at rest and is not claimed as an exposure. The separate memory-vault path (save_memory Tier-1 -> flames_memory.db, plain SQLite) is referenced only as a supporting sentence in vuln-0008 impact because a sibling agent owns memory-vault findings.

entries.surface: Credential-bearing endpoints: chat_datasource, voice_output_service TTS, gateway_client auth frame, server_profile_probe
entries.risk_area: Credential transmitted over cleartext transport (http:// / ws://)
entries.evidence: Filed as vuln-0009 (low, CVSS 3.1, confidence medium): every endpoint validator admits cleartext (lib/domain/services/gateway/gateway_url.dart:15; lib/domain/tools/pairing/pairing_parser.dart:53-56; lib/presentation/screen/settings/cubit/settings_cubit.dart:118-121; lib/presentation/screen/server_profiles/cubit/server_profile_cubit.dart:97-100) and the credential is attached to the resulting endpoint (lib/data/datasources/remote/chat/chat_datasource.dart:38-51 Bearer header; lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/voice_output_service.dart:255-258; lib/data/datasources/remote/gateway/gateway_client.dart:148-155 http->ws rewrite + :211-216 token as first frame), with the project's own docs recommending http:// LAN/Tailscale endpoints (docs/connecting-to-remote-hermes.md:161,176). Report carries the inline fix and names the unresolved runtime question (whether the Flutter engine transmits cleartext on API 26/27) as its proof gap.
