entries.risk_area: Filter bypass — binary/null-byte screening skipped on the PDF code path
entries.evidence: readFile dispatches to the PDF branch BEFORE either content filter runs: `if (ext == 'pdf') { return extractPdfText(path) ... }` at file_workspace_service.dart:159-163 precedes the `_binaryExtensions.contains(ext) || _containsNullByte(bytes)` check at :165. extractPdfText (:178-211) reads via readAsBytes and applies neither filter. Consequence: any file addressed under a `.pdf` name is read with no binary screening. This is a genuine defect in the filter ordering, reported as part of vuln-0007; not independently exploitable beyond the missing containment, since the same path is reachable without the .pdf extension for text files.
entries.recorded_by: Arbitrary File Read Via Device File Tools

entries.risk_area: Scheme/transport allowlist — cleartext ws:// accepted for a credential-bearing socket
entries.evidence: RESOLVED by the cleartext-transport work. Confirmed: acceptedGatewayUrlSchemes = {'http','https','ws','wss'} at gateway_url.dart:15 and normalizeGatewayUri rewrites http->ws / prepends ws:// at gateway_client.dart:149-155; GatewayAuthMessage carries the stored token and is sent as the first frame at :211-216. The missing half — whether a ws:// socket actually works at runtime — is now answered: it does. Flutter's dart:io connection gate allows non-https when `mayInsecurelyConnectToAllDomains` is true, that flag defaults true (engine common/settings.h), and it is only cleared by the `--disallow-insecure-connections` switch (shell/common/switches.cc) which the Android embedding at this repo's pinned Flutter revision never passes; Android's cleartext policy is not consulted by this stack at all. Filed as vuln-0009 (medium, CVSS 5.9), which covers this socket and its TLS-only fix.

entries.risk_area: Credential attach without origin validation / redirect following
entries.evidence: RESOLVED, split into its two halves. (a) Origin validation / cleartext: confirmed — `Authorization: Bearer $apiKey` is set at chat_datasource.dart:51 against a string-concatenated `$baseUrl/chat/completions` (:39), and the base URL is only ever validated by predicates that admit http:// (gateway_url.dart:15, settings_cubit.dart:117-121, settings_screen.dart:417-420). Cleartext is not blocked at runtime (Flutter's dart:io gate is permissive by default on Android at this repo's pinned revision; Android's cleartext policy is not consulted by this stack) — filed as vuln-0009, medium/CVSS 5.9, with the TLS-only fix inline. (b) Redirect forwarding: ruled out — dart:io's `shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect` strips `authorization`/`cookie` unless scheme+host+port match, so dio's default followRedirects does not leak the key cross-origin.

entries.surface: DioTtsClient.synthesize (lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/voice_output_service.dart:219-272) — Authorization: Bearer on the TTS request
entries.risk_area: Credential forwarding to a redirect target chosen by the configured base URL (dio followRedirects default)
entries.evidence: RESOLVED for the redirect question this entry was opened on: ruled out. The stored API key attached to the TTS request (voice_output_service.dart:255-258) is not forwarded across a cross-origin redirect, because dart:io's `shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect` strips the `authorization` header unless the redirect target is same-scheme/host/port. The separate cleartext-transport exposure of the same request (a non-TLS stored base URL, not a redirect) is real and is filed as vuln-0009 (medium, CVSS 5.9) together with the TLS-only fix covering this client.

entries.surface: Pairing destination scheme validation (pairing_parser.dart:53-62, server_profile_cubit.dart:97-107, gateway_client.dart:141-164) vs AndroidManifest cleartext configuration
entries.risk_area: Cleartext transport / ws:// downgrade for the pairing token (http accepted with no https-only enforcement)
entries.evidence: RESOLVED — the consequence this entry could not establish from the repository is now established. Cleartext ws:// (and http://) connections are permitted at runtime on this app's stack: Flutter's dart:io connection gate is permissive by default and the Android embedding never enables strict mode (dart:io `_httpConnectionHook` default allow in embedder_config.dart; engine `_getHttpConnectionHookClosure` in lib/ui/hooks.dart allowing when `mayInsecurelyConnectToAllDomains || uri.isScheme('https')`; `may_insecurely_connect_to_all_domains = true` default in common/settings.h; strict mode only via the `--disallow-insecure-connections` switch in shell/common/switches.cc, which the Android embedding does not pass at the pinned revision). Android's cleartext policy is not consulted by this path. Combined with the code facts already recorded here (pairing_parser.dart:53-56 accepts http; server_profile_cubit.dart:97-107 accepts http; gateway_client.dart:149-155 rewrites http->ws and :211-216 sends the token as the first frame), the pairing token and stored LLM key do travel in cleartext to a cleartext-configured or QR-supplied http origin. Filed as vuln-0009 (medium, CVSS 5.9); the QR origin-redirection aspect remains a separate precondition owned by its own finding.

entries.surface: Non-QR routes to the base-URL/key write primitive
entries.risk_area: Alternative configuration-write routes (manual paste, Add-Profile form, intent extras, share target, gateway RPC) with weaker destination validation
entries.evidence: No alternative route sets a destination with weaker validation, and none can pair a new URL with an old key. Manual JSON paste funnels into the same `_handleBarcode` (qr_scanner_screen.dart:170-258, submit at :250) so it inherits the identical parse+persist path. The Add-Profile form (add_profile_screen.dart:411-425) requires URL and token in the same submit and passes `makeActive: false`, so its new profile is not synced to the active settings unless it becomes the first profile or is later activated — and activation always syncs both fields (`setActiveServerProfile` secure_storage_service.dart:281-288). `MainActivity.extractActionFromIntent` (MainActivity.kt:73-85) reads only `extra_flames_action`; the value reaches a fixed three-string switch (voice_turn_action_listener.dart:162-178) with no default branch, so no intent extra can reach `saveBaseUrl`/`saveApiKey` (grep: no `getStringExtra` other than action/title/content in the whole Kotlin tree). The share path (share_target_cubit.dart:42-48, share_target_service.dart:95-118) only maps shared content into a chat prompt. Gateway RPC frames (gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:68-176) dispatch only to `toolRegistry.executeTool`, and no registered tool writes base URL or key (repo-wide grep for `saveBaseUrl|saveApiKey|saveSettings` over lib/domain + lib/data/datasources/tools is empty).

entries.risk_area: Server-driven credential re-pointing on reconnect / redirect frame
entries.evidence: Reconnect reuses the locally stored URL/token: `_triggerReconnect` (gateway_client.dart:376-380) calls `connect(_currentGatewayUrl!, token: _currentToken)` from local fields; no frame type in `lib/domain/entities/gateway/gateway_message.dart:16-81` carries a URL, host, or profile change (only auth/auth_success/auth_failure/ping/pong/text_delta/tool_call_request/tool_call_response/tool_event/elicitation_request/elicitation_response/chat_message/tool_manifest/error/chat_cancel/raw), and `GatewayRawMessage` (:422-435) is never re-sent by the client (`sendJson` is only called with locally-constructed messages at :386). No server-driven re-pointing exists.

entries.surface: Dio configuration (lib/common/injection/modules.dart) and all HTTP/WS client construction
entries.risk_area: TLS certificate validation disabled / trust store bypass
entries.evidence: Searched the whole tree for TLS overrides: no `badCertificateCallback`, `onBadCertificate`, `setTrustedCertificates`, `SecurityContext`, `HttpOverrides`, `onHttpClientCreate`, or `createHttpClient` in `lib/` or `android/`; the only hits are `lib/common/failure_message.dart:69` and a test asserting a humanized message. The shared Dio (`lib/common/injection/modules.dart:14-17`) sets only connectTimeout/receiveTimeout and registers no interceptors. Certificate validation therefore runs dart:io defaults against the system trust store. No `wss`->`ws` downgrade on reconnect (see reconnect entry).

entries.risk_area: SSE parser injection / unbounded buffering / script execution from remote text
entries.evidence: `SseParser.parse` (sse_parser.dart:78-106) only accepts lines whose trimmed form starts with the literal `data:` (:88), takes the substring after it (:92), and passes it to `jsonDecode` inside a try that swallows only FormatException (:97-102). The caller splits the byte stream on newlines first (chat_datasource.dart:63-68), so a crafted `data:` payload cannot escape JSON parsing into an interpreter, and unparseable frames are dropped. The stream is consumed incrementally by the Dio ResponseBody stream (chat_datasource.dart:38,63) rather than buffered to completion; the model's delta content is rendered through `MarkdownBody` (chat_screen.dart:2078, 2175, 2218) which emits Flutter widgets and does not execute HTML/JS — no WebView is used anywhere (no webview dependency in pubspec.yaml).

entries.risk_area: Inbound frame type with unexpected side effect (URL fetch, profile change, file write)
entries.evidence: Enumerated every inbound frame type in gateway_message.dart:16-81 and traced each side effect: `tool_call_request`/`tool_call` -> tool execution (covered by the dedicated SSRF candidate); `elicitation_request` -> UI approval only, auto-rejected on timeout (gateway_rpc_cubit.dart:191-215); `text_delta`/`chat_message`/`tool_event`/`error` -> UI state and `MarkdownBody` text only (chat_screen.dart:288-362); `ping` -> pong; `auth_*` -> connection state. No frame type carries a URL, profile mutation, or file path (verified by grep for url/baseUrl/gatewayUrl in the entity file: zero hits), so no frame can redirect a credential or trigger a fetch to a frame-supplied destination. The one real privilege crossing is the tool-call path, handled separately.

entries.risk_area: Credential attach without origin validation (connection probe)
entries.evidence: Resolved by enumerating all callers: `ServerProfileProbeService` is only reached from `add_profile_screen.dart:361-393` (`_onTestConnection`, the explicit user-initiated "Test connection" button), and `probeService` is constructed solely at `injection.dart:24-27`. The credential passed in is the value the user just typed into the token field (`add_profile_screen.dart:363,387,389`) — no stored secret is ever fed to it. So there is no silent-exfiltration path here: the user chooses the origin and supplies the credential in the same action, which is the normal, intended behavior of a connection test. Not a vulnerability.

entries.risk_area: Stored API key attached to a stored base URL with no origin binding
entries.evidence: Resolved by adjacent work. The redirect half is ruled out: dart:io's shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect strips authorization on cross-origin redirects, confirmed by the cleartext lane (entry 98ec17). The cleartext half is filed as vuln-0009 (credentials over http:///ws://, incl. the TTS endpoint), and entry efff3e covers this exact sink. What remains is the general "stored key attached to a stored URL with no origin binding" property, which is the same defect already reported for the chat path — there is no separate defect in the TTS client beyond it, and the stored URL/key can only be written through the user-driven settings and profile flows (settings_cubit.dart:117-121, server_profile_cubit.dart:97-107), both of which require http/https with a non-empty host. Not re-filed to avoid duplicating vuln-0009.

entries.risk_area: SSRF / missing authorization gate on Tier-2 tool
entries.evidence: Registered tier2Permission with NO checkPermission field; executeTool (tool_registry.dart:250-255) requires `checkPermission != null` to evaluate the tier, so the Tier-2 gate is short-circuited and the tool auto-executes. agent_cubit.dart:753-765 only pauses for tier3Hitl. validateUrl (domain url_reader_service.dart:59-70) accepts any http/https host with no IP denylist. Verified by executing the verbatim validator in a Dart 3.6 runtime: 127.0.0.1, localhost, 169.254.169.254, 10.0.2.2, 192.168.1.100, 172.16.x, [::1], ::ffff:127.0.0.1, decimal/hex IP forms all return null (ALLOWED).

entries.risk_area: SSRF / redirect-target validation bypass
entries.evidence: fetchUrl sets followRedirects: true with no per-hop validation; validateUrl is only invoked once in fetchReadableText (line 73) on the initial URL. Executed redirect-resolution probe confirms a public initial URL resolving to http://127.0.0.1:8644/rpc, http://169.254.169.254/..., https://192.168.1.100/ and //127.0.0.1/admin would each be followed without revalidation under the pre-fix code.

entries.risk_area: Untrusted-input validation / missing destination allowlist (paste path bypasses camera-only controls)
entries.evidence: Confirmed as a component of vuln-0012. `_showManualInputDialog` (lib/presentation/screen/pairing/qr_scanner_screen.dart:170-258) reads pasted text into a TextField and its Submit button calls `_handleBarcode(text)` at :250, so a pasted payload traverses the identical `PairingParser.parse` path as a camera scan and is subject to the same single scheme check (pairing_parser.dart:53-56). No additional validation, warning, or origin display exists in the dialog (its only controls are Cancel at :230-237 and Submit at :238-253). Consequence for remediation: any control added only to the camera flow would remain bypassable by pasting, so both entry points plus the Settings path must share the fix.

entries.surface: Non-QR base-URL configuration writers (settings reset, Add-Profile form, exported-activity extras, gateway RPC tools)
entries.risk_area: Weaker-validation alternative path to set the active base URL (deep link / exported activity / gateway RPC / manual form)
entries.evidence: Ruled out by enumerating every writer of the gateway destination. `saveBaseUrl(`/`saveApiKey(` appear in lib/ only as matched pairs: secure_storage_service.dart:139-140 (saveSettings) and :283-284 (setActiveServerProfile), and server_profile_cubit.dart:141-142 (addProfile, both from the same payload), plus the settings reset to defaults at settings_cubit.dart:192-197. No registered tool writes the base URL or API key (grep for saveBaseUrl|saveApiKey|saveSettings over lib/domain and lib/data/datasources/tools is empty), so the paired gateway cannot re-point the destination through the tool channel. The exported MainActivity path surfaces only a fixed three-value action allowlist consumed by VoiceTurnActionListener, with no extra reaching storage. The Add-Profile form uses the stricter shared predicate `isAcceptableGatewayUrl` (lib/domain/services/gateway/gateway_url.dart:39-52, called at add_profile_screen.dart:163 and :365), which is user-typed rather than payload-supplied. No deep link or intent filter sets a server profile.

entries.risk_area: Tool enablement / remote skill influence on gate state
entries.evidence: read_web_page is enabled by default (tool_registry.dart:208-211 `putIfAbsent(name, () => true)`; `isToolEnabled` defaults true at :220) and is named in NO skill's `tools:` list, so syncWithToolRegistry (skills_registry_service.dart:386-405) can only ever *enable* it — the disable branch requires the tool to belong to an inactive skill. Remote skill import forces `isEnabled: false` (skill_security_scanner.dart:189-190), so a remote skill cannot self-enable. Net: no enablement control blocks the tool; this supports the SSRF finding rather than ruling it out.

entries.surface: Notification text → tool result → agent prompt (FlamesNotificationListenerService.kt → agent_cubit.dart:820-930)
entries.risk_area: Prompt injection / instruction-data confusion in tool results
entries.evidence: Traced notification text end to end: FlamesNotificationListenerService.kt:62-90 (title/text from Notification.EXTRA_TITLE/EXTRA_TEXT) → MainActivity.kt:124-128 → notification_triage_service.dart:53-65 → tool result → agent_cubit.dart:820-825 `ChatMessage(role:'tool')` → chat_message.dart:116-127 → agent_cubit.dart:906-930 to the remote LLM. No untrusted-data delimiter, wrapper, or sanitization at any hop; tool results are framed only by the JSON `role` field. Covered by a sibling agent's report vuln-0010 (medium, notification→Tier-1 tools), so not re-filed here to avoid duplication.

entries.surface: read_web_page tool result → next ReAct iteration (agent_cubit.dart:820-930)
entries.risk_area: Indirect prompt injection via fetched remote content
entries.evidence: Fetched page text is returned verbatim (capText only truncates; htmlToPlainText only strips markup) and appended as an unframed `role:'tool'` message at agent_cubit.dart:820-825, then serialized by chat_message.dart:116-127 and sent to the remote LLM at agent_cubit.dart:906-930. A page the agent is asked to read can therefore carry instructions into the next ReAct iteration (indirect prompt injection) in addition to being the SSRF exfiltration sink. Recorded as part of vuln-0013's chain rather than as a separate report.

entries.risk_area: SSRF — model/gateway-supplied URL reaching loopback/RFC1918/link-local/metadata
entries.evidence: Adversarial refutation pass found NO chain-breaking control, and the finding is now filed as vuln-0013 (SSRF via read_web_page, low/CVSS 3.7, CWE-918, confidence medium). The refutation checker confirmed: (a) no disable path — `_toolEnabledStates` defaults true (tool_registry.dart:210,222) and `syncWithToolRegistry` (skills_registry_service.dart:386-405) only ever enables; (b) no host/IP denylist, allowlist or Dio interceptor anywhere in lib/; (c) no UI confirmation for Tier-2 (WaitingApproval fires only for tier3Hitl, agent_cubit.dart:753). The validator executed the real `validateUrl` logic in a Dart runtime and it accepted 127.0.0.1, localhost, 169.254.169.254, 10.0.2.2, RFC1918 ranges, [::1], [::ffff:127.0.0.1] and decimal/hex spellings. Recorded as reported so the ledger does not leave an open item next to its own resolution.
entries.recorded_by: Tool Tier Gate And Prompt Injection

entries.surface: Credential-bearing endpoints: chat_datasource, voice_output_service (TTS), gateway_client auth frame, server_profile_probe + their four URL validators
entries.risk_area: Cleartext transmission of credentials (CWE-319) — API key and gateway bearer token over http:// / ws://
entries.evidence: Cleartext transport is LIVE, not fail-closed, and the credentials are attached to it. (1) Credential sinks re-verified line by line: chat_datasource.dart:39/51 (`POST $baseUrl/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer $apiKey`), voice_output_service.dart:255-258 (stored key attached to the TTS endpoint), server_profile_probe_service_impl.dart:23/70 (token attached to a user-typed URL, reached only from the explicit "Test connection" button at add_profile_screen.dart:365), gateway_client.dart:212-216 (gateway token as the first WebSocket frame). Full grep of lib/ + android/ for `Bearer`/`Authorization` returns exactly these four sites — no fifth site. (2) Every validator admits cleartext: gateway_url.dart:15 ({'http','https','ws','wss'}), pairing_parser.dart:53-56, settings_cubit.dart:117-121, server_profile_cubit.dart:97-100, settings_screen.dart:417-420. (3) Deployment guide instructs plain-http: docs/connecting-to-remote-hermes.md:161 (http://100.x.y.z:8642/v1), :176 (http://192.168.1.100:8642/v1), :284. (4) Platform layer does NOT block it: dart:io's `_httpConnectionHook` defaults to allow (sdk/lib/_http/embedder_config.dart), Flutter's replacement gate allows when `mayInsecurelyConnectToAllDomains || uri.isScheme('https')` (engine lib/ui/hooks.dart), the flag defaults true (engine common/settings.h) and is only cleared by `--disallow-insecure-connections` (shell/common/switches.cc), which the Android embedding at this repo's pinned revision never passes (verified by git grep at that revision); the old opt-in `io.flutter.network-policy` manifest mechanism was removed upstream. dio reaches this stack via its IO adapter (HttpClient()), and WebSocket.connect reuses the same HttpClient, so ws:// is covered too. Filed as vuln-0009, revised to medium/CVSS 5.9 with the corrected mechanism and the inline TLS-only fix.

entries.surface: chat_datasource / voice_output_service / probe redirect handling (followRedirects default true)
entries.risk_area: Credential forwarding across a cross-origin redirect
entries.evidence: Checked whether the credential could leak through a redirect. dart:io's `_HttpClient.shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect` (sdk/lib/_http/http_impl.dart, `_openUrlFromRequest`) strips `authorization`, `www-authenticate`, `proxy-authorization`, `proxy-authenticate`, `cookie` and `cookie2` unless `_isSameOrigin` (scheme + host + port all equal) holds — so an `https` credential request redirected to a third-party origin does NOT carry the bearer token. This closes the "open redirect leaks the key" variant. Note this does not help the cleartext case (that is a direct request to a non-TLS origin, filed as vuln-0009). dio's default `followRedirects: true` therefore does not add a separate credential-exfil path here.

entries.surface: All outbound gateway/LLM send paths (gateway_client.dart sendJson/sendChatMessage + callers)
entries.risk_area: Sending credentials to a URL taken from an inbound message
entries.evidence: Traced every outbound gateway send: `sendJson` (gateway_client.dart:391-394) is only ever called with locally constructed messages (auth frame :216, pong :263, tool manifest :303, tool responses :399-423, chat :427-437, cancel :441-443), and `sendChatMessage` has exactly two callers (`chat_screen.dart:1522` gated on `client.state.isConnected`, and `gateway_voice_prompt_dispatcher.dart:74`). No outbound frame destination or credential is derived from an inbound frame, and no frame type carries a URL/host (verified by grep against `lib/domain/entities/gateway/gateway_message.dart`: zero hits for url/baseUrl/gatewayUrl). The only URL-bearing outbound calls are the local LLM/TTS clients, whose base URL comes from secure storage, not from the socket.

entries.surface: All credential-attach sites (gateway auth frame, chat/TTS Authorization headers, WS handshake)
entries.risk_area: Credential leakage via URL query string / handshake header / Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
entries.evidence: No credential is ever placed in a URL or header by the transport layer: the gateway token is sent only as the `token` field of the `auth` JSON frame (gateway_client.dart:212-216), and the LLM/TTS clients use an `Authorization: Bearer` header (chat_datasource.dart:51, voice_output_service.dart:258, probe service :23/:70). Grep for query-string/token-parameter patterns and `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` across `lib/` returns no credential-carrying usage; `IoGatewaySocketFactory.connect` (gateway_socket.dart:69-74) passes only caller-supplied headers and the app supplies none. Note dart:io itself would convert URL userinfo into a Basic auth header (websocket_impl.dart), but `isAcceptableGatewayUrl`/`normalizeGatewayUri` never require or add userinfo, so that path is not exercised by app-controlled input.

entries.risk_area: Path traversal / arbitrary file write via an auto-executing Tier-1 file-writing tool
entries.evidence: `export_document_pdf` (lib/data/datasources/skills/doc_builder_skill.dart:33-71) is registered at `securityTier: SecurityTier.tier1Auto` (:62) and wired manually at injection.config.dart:391-392, so it auto-executes with no gate — it belongs to the Tier-1 misclassification family already filed as vuln-0005. However the path-traversal angle is ruled out by a named control: the output filename is built by `_slugify` (doc_builder_skill.dart:125-132) which lowercases and replaces every character outside `[a-z0-9]` with `_`, then strips leading/trailing underscores and caps at 60 chars, before joining to `<documents dir>/documents/doc_<slug>_<stamp>.pdf` (:91-97). Model-controlled `title` and `outputFileName` therefore cannot inject `/`, `..`, or a separator into the path, and the write target is confined to the app documents directory via `getDocumentsDirectory()`. No traversal or arbitrary-write impact.
entries.recorded_by: Tool Tier Gate And Prompt Injection

entries.risk_area: Other credential-in-transit shapes: query-string tokens, credentials in logcat, TLS verification weakening
entries.evidence: Swept for other credential-in-transit shapes. (a) Query-string credentials: grep across lib/ for `?token=`, `?api_key=`, `api_key=`, `access_token` returns ZERO hits — every credential is carried in a header (`Authorization: Bearer`, chat_datasource.dart:51, voice_output_service.dart:258, server_profile_probe_service_impl.dart:23/70) or in the WebSocket auth frame (gateway_client.dart:212-216), never in a URL. This matters because a query-string token would additionally land in server logs and referrers. (b) Logcat: grep for `Log.`, `println`, `printStackTrace`, `System.out` across android/app/src/main/kotlin/ returns zero hits, so no Kotlin component writes a credential to logcat; the Dart-side log sites are covered by the parent's entry 1689c2. (c) TLS verification: no `badCertificateCallback`, `onBadCertificate`, `setTrustedCertificates`, `SecurityContext`, `HttpOverrides` or custom `HttpClientAdapter` anywhere in lib/ or android/ (only a `DioExceptionType.badCertificate` case in failure_message.dart:68), so https/wss requests use the platform trust store unweakened. (d) Full enumeration of `Bearer`/`Authorization` in lib/ + android/ returns exactly four sites, all accounted for above — no fifth credential sink.

entries.surface: Share content:// provider path traversal (plugin FileDirectory via receive_sharing_intent 1.9.0) → lib/domain/services/share/share_target_service.dart mapFile
entries.risk_area: Path Traversal / arbitrary app-private file write from an untrusted content:// provider
entries.evidence: CONFIRMED (static + offline harness). Chain: manifest MainActivity exported=true no permission (AndroidManifest.xml:57-116, SEND/SEND_MULTIPLE filters accept type=*/* and image/*) → plugin handleIntent media branch requires intent.type != null (ReceiveSharingIntentPlugin.kt:86-89) → getMediaUris → FileDirectory.getAbsolutePath (ReceiveSharingIntentPlugin.kt:141) → getDataColumn uri.authority!=null branch takes provider-supplied `_display_name` with NO sanitisation (FileDirectory.kt:95, :102-104) → File(context.cacheDir, fileName) → FileOutputStream(targetFile) copies provider stream (FileDirectory.kt:123-127). JVM Unix resolve concatenates, so `../` escapes cacheDir at syscall time; verified by offline harness (write landed in databases/ outside cache) and a real compiled Dart check of the guard. No sanitisation exists anywhere in the plugin (grep sanitiz|normaliz|canonical|validate → only mimeType startsWith checks). Report filed.
entries.recorded_by: Validate Share Provider Path Traversal Write

entries.surface: MainActivity ACTION_VIEW content:// BROWSABLE filter (AndroidManifest.xml:109-115) reaching the vulnerable plugin branch
entries.risk_area: Deep-link (BROWSABLE) reachability of the share file-copy sink
entries.evidence: RULED OUT as an independent path: the plugin's media branch (ReceiveSharingIntentPlugin.kt:86-89) requires intent.type != null; a browser ACTION_VIEW for content:// arrives with type null and falls through to the URL branch (:98-107), which only forwards intent.dataString as a URL and never calls FileDirectory. The exploitable entry is therefore ACTION_SEND / ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE with a non-null type, which the manifest's text/*, image/* and */* filters accept (AndroidManifest.xml:78-108). Not filed as a separate finding; recorded as a narrowing of the attack surface, not a blocker.
entries.recorded_by: Validate Share Provider Path Traversal Write

entries.surface: lib/data/datasources/tools/chat/piper_tts_engine.dart:233-249 (Piper voice tarball extraction loop) — content-integrity and abort-state behaviour
entries.risk_area: Archive content integrity / entry-boundary confusion (declared size vs actual data, entry-skip via removeFile, mid-loop abort state)
entries.evidence: Executed a hand-crafted tar whose entry declares `fileSize` far larger than the data actually present (declared 4096 / 2560 bytes, supplied 5 bytes). Observed decoder behaviour: `TarFile.read` (tar_file.dart:96-113) consumes the declared byte count from the stream, so the entry's content absorbs the following tar header(s) and the next entry's data — the written file was 2560 bytes containing `AAAAA` + a verbatim tar header + `BBBBB`. No security impact and no escape: the write still lands under `<modelsRoot>/<voiceId>/` (guards at piper_tts_engine.dart:240-244 unchanged), the attacker must already fully control the archive bytes so re-synchronising to a chosen header grants nothing they did not already have, and an entry swallowed this way is simply never written (skipping cannot bypass a pre-write guard). Additionally the archive bytes cannot be attacker-chosen at all in practice: the MD5 gate at piper_tts_engine.dart:221-228 compares against a compile-time constant digest (piper_voice.dart:34/45/56) over a hardcoded HTTPS GitHub URL. Also verified the loop's `archive.removeFile(entry)` over `archive.files.toList()` (a defensive copy — archive.dart:16 `UnmodifiableListView`, :40-47 `removeFile`) cannot cause an entry to be skipped: executed with 3- and 5-entry archives, all entries seen and processed. A mid-loop `writeAsBytes` failure (file-then-file-under-that-file, errno 20 ENOTDIR) throws out of the loop, but the `finally` only deletes the tmp tarball and the leftover partial directory is inside the app-private models root. Residual, not a finding: `tarballSizeBytes` (piper_voice.dart:10) is declared but never enforced anywhere, so a compromised/malicious release server could serve an arbitrarily large body into the app-private dir — already recorded separately and not reachable without defeating TLS + the pinned MD5.

entries.risk_area: Arbitrary file read via provider-supplied _data absolute path
entries.evidence: Assessed as a read primitive and rejected: FileDirectory.kt:131-144 (the uri.authority == null branch) returns a provider-supplied `_data` value with no copy, but a `content://` URI without an authority makes ContentResolver.query throw rather than return attacker data, and normal `content://` URIs always carry an authority (so they take the authority != null branch at :93). No path in this app produces an authority-less content:// URI. Additionally the value only ever reaches SharedPayload.value (share_target_service.dart:105-114) and is never opened by the Dart layer as a file - grep for File(payload / File(.*\.value) returns nothing. Not reported.
entries.recorded_by: Validate Share Provider Path Traversal Write

entries.surface: Arbitrary app-private file write → code execution escalation (dex/so/native loading)
entries.risk_area: Escalation of the app-private file write to code execution
entries.evidence: No code path executes or dynamically loads anything from a writable app-private directory: grep of lib/ and android/app/src/main/kotlin/ for Process.start, Runtime.getRuntime, DexClassLoader, System.load, DynamicLibrary.open and dart:ffi returns zero matches. Artifacts under databases/, shared_prefs/ and app_flutter/ (Hive) are opened as data only. The impact of the traversal is therefore data integrity, not code execution - stated explicitly in the filed report so the severity is not over-rated.
entries.recorded_by: Validate Share Provider Path Traversal Write

entries.surface: MainActivity SEND / SEND_MULTIPLE / VIEW content:// intent filters (manifest:78-115)
entries.risk_area: Third-party reachable exported component attack surface (overall)
entries.evidence: MainActivity declares SEND/SEND_MULTIPLE filters for text/*, image/*, */* (manifest:78-108) and a VIEW content:// BROWSABLE filter (manifest:110-115). All three resulting attack paths were validated and filed: (1) action-extra injection → vuln-0003; (2) share-text auto-submit to agent + attacker-chosen URL fetch → vuln-0011; (3) content:// provider _display_name path traversal write → vuln-0014. No caller-identity check exists on any path (rg getCallingActivity|getCallingPackage|Binder.getCallingUid = 0 hits).

entries.surface: Flutter MethodChannel / EventChannel surface (all channels in MainActivity.kt and plugins)
entries.risk_area: Cross-app reachability of Flutter platform channels / deep links
entries.evidence: All MethodChannel/EventChannel names in the app are in-process Flutter binary-messenger channels (MainActivity.kt:31-39 defines nine, plus the plugin's receive_sharing_intent/messages and events-media). They are reachable only from the app's own Dart code; a third-party Android app has no handle on the binary messenger and cannot invoke a channel handler directly. The only way a foreign app can influence them is by starting an exported component, which is exactly the three validated paths already filed (vuln-0003/0011/0014). No getInitialLink / uni_links / app_links deep-link plugin is present in pubspec.yaml; the only deep-link-shaped surface is the manifest VIEW content:// filter, covered under the traversal and share findings.

entries.risk_area: Untrusted role field from a remote frame injected as a system-role LLM instruction
entries.evidence: Filed as vuln-0016 (medium, CVSS 4.2, CWE-863, confidence medium) with the inline fix (parse-boundary role allowlist at gateway_message.dart:358-364). The unvalidated role parse is the root control; verbatim storage (chat_screen.dart:311-316), persistence and reload (agent_cubit.dart:185-189, :330-352), survival of the mode switch (chat_screen.dart:1084-1112), and unfiltered serialization into the model request (agent_cubit.dart:906, chat_message.dart:116-119) complete the chain. Static trace only — no runtime execution was possible.

entries.risk_area: Privileged frame dispatch before authentication completes (missing auth-state guard)
entries.evidence: Filed as vuln-0015 (medium, CVSS 4.8, CWE-306, confidence medium) with the inline fix. The missing authenticated-state guard in _handleIncomingData (gateway_client.dart:240-284) is the root control; the pre-auth dispatch of tool_call_request/elicitation_request to the device RPC receiver (gateway_client.dart:269-277 -> gateway_rpc_cubit.dart:127-139 -> gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:89,148) is the sink; the repo's own test at gateway_rpc_cubit_test.dart:401-417 independently confirms the listener is active during connecting. Static trace only — no runtime execution was possible.

entries.risk_area: Credential exposure via WebSocket handshake redirect (origin binding)
entries.evidence: Confirmed: WebSocket.connect is called without a customClient (gateway_socket.dart:71-74), dart:io defaults _followRedirects=true/_maxRedirects=5 and follows 301/302/303/307/308 for GET; the redirect target completes the upgrade and GatewayClient sends the auth frame (gateway_client.dart:212-216) to it. Reproduced live with a Dart 3.13.3 PoC: token delivered to the redirect target, including a wss:// -> http:// cleartext downgrade. Filed as a vulnerability report.
entries.recorded_by: Gateway Cleartext And Redirect Token Exposure Validator

entries.risk_area: Cleartext transport of stored bearer token (ws:// / http://)
entries.evidence: Confirmed: acceptedGatewayUrlSchemes includes http/ws (gateway_url.dart:15) and isAcceptableGatewayUrl only checks scheme membership + non-empty host (gateway_url.dart:39-52); normalizeGatewayUri rewrites http->ws (gateway_client.dart:149-150); no warning anywhere in the UI. Cleartext reaches the wire because the pinned engine revision (a804b261645ef8c13eb3d5c44a5c2fb0340c5539) defaults may_insecurely_connect_to_all_domains=true (settings.h:167), only clears it via --disallow-insecure-connections (switches.cc:269-270), and the Android embedder never passes that flag (FlutterShellArgs.java contains no such argument; FlutterApplicationInfo.domainNetworkPolicy defaults to ""). Docs recommend cleartext for LAN. Filed as a vulnerability report.
entries.recorded_by: Gateway Cleartext And Redirect Token Exposure Validator

entries.risk_area: Prompt injection / untrusted instruction-context injection (system-role planting via inbound gateway frame)
entries.evidence: Filed as a vulnerability report. Inbound `chat_message` frames carry an attacker-chosen `role` string straight through GatewayChatMessage.fromJson (gateway_message.dart:361) with no allowlist; chat_screen.dart:311-316 persists it via AgentCubit.addMessage (agent_cubit.dart:185-189), and agent_cubit.dart:906+917-921 re-serializes it into the OpenAI request via ChatMessage.toWireJson (chat_message.dart:116-127), which emits 'role' verbatim. Executed the real parser + ChatMessage code with the aarch64 Dart SDK: a frame with role=system produced a second system-authority entry in the outgoing messages array. Refutation attempt (gateway turns answered server-side so poisoned history never reaches the LLM) was tested and FAILED: _handleVoiceSubmitted (chat_screen.dart:1547-1556) calls AgentCubit.sendMessage regardless of _mode, and the poisoned message is persisted and reloaded on the direct-mode path.
entries.recorded_by: Gateway Frame System-Role Context Injection Validator

entries.surface: Inbound gateway `tool_call_request` frame -> GatewayDeviceRpcReceiver -> read_web_page -> UrlReaderService.fetchReadableText (gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:89,:148,:167-179; gateway_client.dart:269-277)
entries.risk_area: SSRF / Tier-2 gate bypass via an inbound gateway RPC frame, with the fetched body returned to the frame sender
entries.evidence: CONFIRMED as a second trigger path and folded into vuln-0013 (revised). Independent verification of all nine evidence points succeeded and the refutation sweep failed to find a chain-breaking control: gateway_message.dart:280-293 takes `tool`+`arguments` from the wire with no validation; gateway_client.dart:269-277 routes the frame to `_toolCallRequestController` whenever a listener is attached; gateway_rpc_cubit.dart:85-91 subscribes and :127-139 passes `onApprovalRequired: _requestHitlApproval`; gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:89 gates ONLY `requiresHitl` (Tier 3) so Tier-2 `read_web_page` (tool_registry.dart:1548) proceeds unapproved to executeTool at :148; tool_registry.dart:250-256 skips the permission block when `checkPermission` is null, which it is for read_web_page; url_reader_service.dart:59-70 accepts any http/https host with no loopback/RFC1918/link-local/metadata denylist and :47 follows redirects unrevalidated. The gateway route is materially stronger than the ReAct route because the fetched body is returned directly to the frame's sender (gateway_rpc_receiver.dart:167-179 `sendToolCallResponse(callId: request.id, result: resultMap)`), removing the model from the loop, and the tool is advertised to the server in the handshake manifest (modules.dart:39-40 -> gateway_client.dart:303, filter at tool_registry.dart:233-236 which applies enablement only, no pruning). Listener liveness confirmed: cubit starts listening from its constructor (gateway_rpc_cubit.dart:55, :67-69), the DI factory does not override autoStart (injection.config.dart:462-467), screen resolves it in initState (chat_screen.dart:201-202). Unconfirmed, not dynamically validated — static trace only.
entries.recorded_by: Gateway RPC Tier-2 Gate SSRF Validator

gaps.risk_area: Sensitive data exposure — password field text captured from other apps
gaps.detail: captureTree() never calls AccessibilityNodeInfo.isPassword(); the identifier appears nowhere in the android/ or lib/ trees (repo-wide search). Whether the platform already redacts password text before an accessibility service sees it is device/OEM dependent and could NOT be verified — no device, no emulator, no adb. The missing client-side control is established; actual secret capture is not. Fix included as a second part of vuln-0004 (skips isPassword nodes and their subtrees); device verification of both the gap and the fix remains open.

gaps.surface: Residual Tier-1 side-effecting tools: speak_text, open_map_navigation, list_device_files
gaps.risk_area: Tier-1 misclassification (residual instances not included in the filed fix set)
gaps.detail: Three further Tier-1 tools have side effects but were deliberately excluded from the fix set in vuln-0005 as lower-impact: `speak_text` (tool_registry.dart:1119, tier :1138) speaks arbitrary model text aloud; `open_map_navigation` (:1442, tier :1462) launches an external app via a geo intent; `list_device_files` (:793, tier :809) performs ungated recursive directory enumeration (its file-read aspect is owned by another agent). Same root cause as the reported defect but not remediated by the six tier changes; flagged for follow-up rather than silently dropped.

gaps.surface: AgentCubit._pendingToolCall approval slot (agent_cubit.dart:64, :752-762, :602-614) with unguarded second-turn entry points (share intent, NFC)
gaps.risk_area: HITL approval-gate integrity across concurrent turns (shared pending-approval slot overwrite -> approving one tool may execute another)
gaps.detail: Distinct from the already-recorded single-turn check (entry c8730f, which asked whether the sheet's displayed arguments match the executed ones — they do, same map object). This row is the CROSS-TURN case: approval is bound to the shared mutable slot `_pendingToolCall` (agent_cubit.dart:64) rather than to the request the user is looking at. `_processPendingToolCalls` assigns the slot then emits `WaitingApproval` (:759-761); `approveAction` re-reads the slot (:606-614) and never compares it with `state.request`. A second turn can start while a tier-3 approval is pending because `sendMessage` has no busy/awaiting-approval guard (:502-536, it only bumps `_runGeneration`), and two unguarded entry points reach it — the exported share intent (chat_screen.dart:386-398 -> :531-565 -> :1494+) and the NFC trigger (agent_cubit.dart:561-580). If that second turn also pauses on a tier-3 tool, the slot is overwritten with a different request while the older sheet is still mounted (the listener pushes a new modal at chat_screen.dart:1572-1585 and never dismisses the previous one; the sheet is isDismissible:false / enableDrag:false with PopScope canPop:false at action_approval_sheet.dart:29-48). A tap landing in the window between the overwrite emit and the new sheet being pushed would execute the request that was never displayed. I could NOT name a control that closes this: the `if (state is! WaitingApproval) return;` guard at :603 only covers the case where the state has already left WaitingApproval (e.g. after `stop()`, which nulls the slot at :844 and emits AgentIdle at :846), and it does not detect that the slot was replaced by a different request while the state stayed WaitingApproval. I also could not confirm it — it needs a real device to observe the emit-to-push frame window and to make the model emit a second tier-3 call, and no emulator/adb exists in this environment. Recorded as open rather than ruled out.

gaps.surface: Dynamic validation of read_device_file against app-private storage (databases/flames_memory.db, flames_skills.db)
gaps.risk_area: Runtime confirmation of the readable path set (same-UID access to app-private databases)
gaps.detail: No Android build was possible (no emulator, no adb, no running app, no resolved Dart dependencies), so I could not confirm by execution which absolute paths the app process can actually open at runtime, nor observe a real model-emitted tool call reaching the sink. Android semantics make same-UID reads of the app's own private storage the expected behaviour, but that was not observed. The report (vuln-0007) is filed at confidence=medium with this gap named in confidence_rationale, and it is carried as an open item.
